ozet.about.title: Kettle Works Crew
ozet.about.heading: Industrial Salvagers
ozet.about.blurb: A large salvage gang out of the works yard. Numbers instead of discipline: they arrive together and they swarm.

ozet.about.title: Kentucky Guard - 149th Armored Bde
ozet.about.heading: Military Holdouts
ozet.about.blurb: What is left of a Kentucky Army National Guard detachment of the 149th Armored Brigade. They hold their range, work in lanes, and treat a firefight as a job rather than a fight.

ozet.about.title: 101st Airborne - Knox Cordon Detachment
ozet.about.heading: Military Quarantine Force
ozet.about.blurb: The Army's line round the Exclusion Zone, drawn by the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault) out of Fort Campbell, still standing where the order left it. Masks on, plates in, ammunition that does not run out: they hold the bridge, and nothing crosses it twice.

ozet.about.title: Knox County Deputies
ozet.about.heading: Law Remnant
ozet.about.blurb: Deputies still running the county by their own reading of it. Shotguns at the door, sidearms behind, and an officer who calls the shots.

ozet.about.title: Station 14 Crew
ozet.about.heading: Emergency Services
ozet.about.blurb: A fire crew that never stood down. Axes and one shotgun between them, they move as one body and they carry their wounded out.

ozet.about.title: Riverside Survivors
ozet.about.heading: Civilian Holdouts
ozet.about.blurb: Neighbours who armed themselves. Not soldiers: they scavenge, they stay together, and they break when it turns bad.

ozet.about.title: Post 4 Troopers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: Post 4 troopers still working US-31W in the first week: roadblocks, missing-person sweeps, a radio that still answers.

ozet.about.title: County Sheriff
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: The county sheriff and what is left of his deputies, holding the courthouse road and the town squares while the county still means something.

ozet.about.title: Muldraugh Police
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: Muldraugh's chief and his two cruisers. Small-town police: they know everybody, and they are not ready for this.

ozet.about.title: Jail Detail
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: The jail detail from the courthouse basement, keeping the lockup and the block around it while the trusties still answer to them.

ozet.about.title: Conservation Officers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: Fish and Wildlife officers on the rivers and in the knobs, the only law in the back country and used to being alone.

ozet.about.title: Courthouse Holdouts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: The clerks and one deputy who never left the courthouse. They keep records nobody will read and a door nobody gets through.

ozet.about.title: Work Crew Runaways
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Law Enforcement
ozet.about.blurb: A roadside work crew that walked off when the officer stopped coming back. Boilersuits under stolen jackets, moving at night.

IGUI_ALifeUI_7203827e7fc942aa.en: US Army Armor School Cadre - Fort Knox

ozet.about.title: US Army Armor School Cadre - Fort Knox
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: US Army Armor Center cadre off Fort Knox, the Armor School instructors and crews, working the 31W corridor in the first week with a helicopter still on call.

ozet.about.title: Fort Knox Military Police Company
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: Fort Knox military police on the roads into the installation: checkpoints, curfew, and a patience that is running out.

ozet.about.title: 149th Armored Brigade - Engineers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: A Kentucky Guard engineer platoon of the 149th Armored Brigade, called up for the bridge works and the road blocks. Tools, trucks, and one rifle in three.

ozet.about.title: 2nd Bn 123rd Armor - Rifle Detail
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: A Kentucky Army National Guard rifle detail of 2nd Battalion, 123rd Armor -- your neighbours with a drill weekend -- holding a cordon it was told to hold.

IGUI_ALifeUI_4ddbc17b734b43c6.en: United States Mint Police - Vault Detail

ozet.about.title: United States Mint Police - Vault Detail
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: United States Mint Police from the depository. Another service, another uniform, a much smaller number; they answer to nobody here.

ozet.about.title: The Left-Behind
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: The Left-Behind: soldiers who stopped taking orders and kept the rifles. They are not looking for a fight, and they win the ones they get.

ozet.about.title: Volunteer Fire
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: The volunteer fire department, pagers on every belt, still answering calls in the first days because nobody told them to stop.

ozet.about.title: County EMS
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: A county ambulance crew working the highway wrecks until the fuel and the will run out.

ozet.about.title: Hospital Staff
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: Hospital staff holding a ward in Louisville: scrubs, tired eyes, and the only people who still know what to do with a wound.

ozet.about.title: American Red Cross - Relief Column
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: A relief column that made it into the county: cots, water and a coordinator with a clipboard, asking where the shelter is.

ozet.about.title: The Station
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: The Station: three people, a transmitter and a generator, still on the air for whoever is listening.

ozet.about.title: Line Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: A utility line crew caught out on a service road with the bucket truck, trying to get home.

ozet.about.title: Vittitoe Barns
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Vittitoe Barns: six hundred acres of burley east of Muldraugh, four brothers, a granary and an armoury. They feed people who work.

ozet.about.title: Renfro Road
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Renfro Road: thirty years of running liquor into a dry county. The road is theirs now, and they charge to use it.

ozet.about.title: Tackett Hollow
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Tackett Hollow: marijuana in the corn, one federal case, nobody talked. Same ground, same silence, more guns.

ozet.about.title: Bledsoe Landing
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Bledsoe Landing: barge deckhands and gravel dredgers at the West Point ramp. They move people and goods on the water, for a price.

ozet.about.title: Prather Congregation
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Prather Congregation: a West Point church that took people in and asks what you believe. They will feed you; they will not arm you.

ozet.about.title: Coyle Pawn
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Coyle Pawn: bought what soldiers sold. The county's fence and gun market; they sell to anyone with something to trade.

ozet.about.title: Ledford Camp
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Ledford Camp: a deer camp and a cockfighting pit in the knobs. Hunters who moved to a new animal, and sporting about it.

ozet.about.title: Kessinger Dairy
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Kessinger Dairy: a big family that walled the milking parlour and took in the cousins. Exhausted, careful, dangerous when pushed.

ozet.about.title: Slaughter Fire Hall
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Slaughter Fire Hall: the chief and two generations of volunteers. They kept the pumper running and put out fires for payment in fuel.

ozet.about.title: Napier Row
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Napier Row: laid off in the drawdown, took the trailer row and the ground it sits on. A chip on every shoulder.

ozet.about.title: Whitaker Elevator
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Whitaker Elevator: bought and dried the county's corn. They own the food and the scales, and they will starve you out.

ozet.about.title: Dabney Practice
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Dabney Practice: a vet and a boarding barn turned holdout. Medicine at a price nobody likes, from the only doctor left in the county.

ozet.about.title: Crume Scrap
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Crume Scrap: crushed cars on 31W, now cutting steel plate for anyone with fuel. They armour the trucks, and themselves.

ozet.about.title: Hobbs Brothers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: The Hobbs brothers: small-time thieves with no home, following other people's fights and taking what is left.

ozet.about.title: The Cornfield Men
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: The Cornfield Men: growers who never had much use for the law and have less now. Patient, hidden, and armed for the harvest.

ozet.about.title: County Line Runners
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: County Line Runners: bootleggers who know every back road between the wet county and the dry one, and who is on them.

ozet.about.title: Dixie Road Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Dixie Road Crew: highway thieves who set the road and wait. When a car stops, they come out of both ditches.

ozet.about.title: Iron Horse Club
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Iron Horse Club: the local motorcycle club, a garage on 31W and a grudge against the Louisville chapters.

ozet.about.title: Derby Street Set
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Derby Street Set: a Louisville corner crew that kept its block when the police stopped coming.

ozet.about.title: Barn Cutters
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Barn Cutters: a chop shop in a tobacco barn. Parts for anything, no questions, cash or fuel.

ozet.about.title: The Pit
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: The Pit: a fighting ring that outgrew its warehouse. Padded, helmeted, and hungry for a crowd.

ozet.about.title: The Toll
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: The Toll: a protection racket dressed up as a militia. One stretch of road, a gate, and a price that goes up.

ozet.about.title: Truck Stop Commune
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: Truck Stop Commune: drivers who were passing through and stayed. Diesel, CB radio, and a lot of guns behind the counter.

ozet.about.title: County Gun Club
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: County Gun Club: people who owned rifles before it was necessary, and know how to use them.

ozet.about.title: The Prepared
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: The Prepared: a family that built the cellar for exactly this, and does not want company.

ozet.about.title: Schoolhouse
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: Schoolhouse: teachers who kept the building and whoever came to it. Friendly, organised, and out of food.

ozet.about.title: Stockyard Co-op
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: Stockyard Co-op: cattlemen who pooled the herds and the feed. Nobody eats for free.

ozet.about.title: Rivermen
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: Rivermen: towboat and barge crews off the Ohio, working the wharfs for whatever floats.

ozet.about.title: Outlaws MC
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Outlaws MC: the Louisville chapter, a clubhouse, and a road they mean to own. Patrols, tolls and fuel runs -- the club has influence, and it wants more.

ozet.about.title: Grim Reapers MC
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Grim Reapers MC: the other Louisville club, a separate clubhouse and an old war with the Outlaws that did not end with the world.

ozet.about.title: Undertakers MC
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Undertakers MC: riders from out of the region, come to see what the Outlaws are holding, and friendly to them.

ozet.about.title: Dixie Mafia - County Contacts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Dixie Mafia contacts: the highway network of thieves and fences from prison days, working the motels on 31W.

ozet.about.title: Cornbread Mafia - Remaining Contacts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Cornbread Mafia remnants: growers from the syndicate years who still know where the patches are and still do not talk.

ozet.about.title: Chicago Outfit - Stranded Contacts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Chicago Outfit contacts stranded in a Louisville motel, with a car, a briefcase and a phone that does not ring.

ozet.about.title: Vice Lords - Stranded Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Vice Lords crew stranded in Louisville: one block, held hard, with I-65 closed behind them.

ozet.about.title: Gangster Disciples - Stranded Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Gangster Disciples crew stranded in Louisville, holding a block of their own and watching the Vice Lords' block.

ozet.about.title: Bloods - Victory Park Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Bloods -- the Victory Park crew. Red on every cap, a set of streets, and a war across the park that outlasted the city.

ozet.about.title: Crips - Victory Park Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: Crips -- the Victory Park crew. Blue on every cap, the other half of the park, the other half of the war.

ozet.about.title: First Family - Stranded Contacts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Clubs and Networks
ozet.about.blurb: First Family contacts: made men who drove down from the north and cannot drive back. Suits, sidearms, and a plan.

ozet.about.title: Rosewood Police
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Rosewood Police: the station by the prison road, three officers and the town.

ozet.about.title: Riverside Police
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Riverside Police: a chief and two officers on the river road.

ozet.about.title: West Point Police
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: West Point Police: the station on the Dixie Highway, holding the town and the river bank.

ozet.about.title: Louisville Division of Police
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Louisville Division of Police: city police inside the city line, and not on speaking terms with the county force.

ozet.about.title: Jefferson County Police
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Jefferson County Police: the county force outside the city line, and not on speaking terms with the city one.

ozet.about.title: KSP Special Response Team
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: KSP Special Response Team: the state police tactical unit, sent in once and never called back.

ozet.about.title: Rosewood Corrections
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Rosewood Corrections: the prison staff who kept the gate, the walls and whoever was inside them.

ozet.about.title: Prison Infirmary Staff
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Prison infirmary staff: two nurses and a doctor behind a locked wing, still treating whoever comes to the door.

ozet.about.title: Prison Shelter Group
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Prison shelter group: inmates who barred a cell block and want nothing but to be left alone in it.

ozet.about.title: Prison Yard Predators
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Prison yard predators: the men the walls were for. Magazines taped over the chest, shivs, and the guards' shotgun.

ozet.about.title: Prison Escape Pair
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: A prison escape pair on the road to the woods, in stolen jackets over prison khaki.

ozet.about.title: Corrections Remnants
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Police and Corrections
ozet.about.blurb: Corrections remnants: guards who held a wing after the state stopped paying, then a house after the wing fell.

ozet.about.title: Trooper Remnants
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Trooper remnants: a post that never got relieved. Grey shirts under civilian coats, still stopping cars on 31W.

ozet.about.title: County Law Remnants
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: County law remnants: deputies running their own county out of a house, the badge still on the belt.

ozet.about.title: Kentucky Guard Remnants - 149th Armored Bde
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Kentucky Guard remnants: a 149th Armored Brigade platoon that stopped taking orders and kept the field depot.

ozet.about.title: 149th Armored Bde - Engineer Holdouts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Engineer holdouts: 149th Armored Brigade Guard engineers who kept the workshop and the generator, and trade repairs for food.

ozet.about.title: 1st Armor Training Brigade Remnants
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Training remnants: a 1st Armor Training Brigade platoon cut off on the range roads, half-trained and led by one sergeant.

ozet.about.title: Conservation Remnants
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Conservation remnants: two officers living out of a forest camp, keeping the woods the way they always did.

ozet.about.title: 149th Armored Bde - Transport Detail
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Guard transport detail of the 149th Armored Brigade: truck drivers with a convoy that went nowhere, guarding what is on the trucks.

ozet.about.title: Ireland Army Hospital - Medical Detail
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Uniformed Remnants
ozet.about.blurb: Army medical detail: a field aid station out of Ireland Army Community Hospital at Fort Knox, treating soldiers first and everybody eventually.

ozet.about.title: Off-Duty Paramedics
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Off-duty paramedics holding a house and a kit bag, still going out when they hear a crash.

ozet.about.title: Ward Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Ward survivors: the patients and one nurse who were on the floor the hospital lost, and kept the ward.

ozet.about.title: Utility Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Utility survivors: a co-op crew holding a workshop, trading generator work for anything that burns.

ozet.about.title: Highway Maintenance Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: The state highway crew, dump trucks and salt shed, still clearing wrecks in the first days.

ozet.about.title: Telephone Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: A two-man telephone crew at a switching point, waiting for a dial tone that is not coming.

ozet.about.title: Waterworks Staff
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Waterworks staff keeping the pumps going as long as the diesel lasts.

ozet.about.title: Sanitation Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: A sanitation crew that kept the truck and the yard. They know every back alley in town.

ozet.about.title: Rail Maintenance Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Rail maintenance survivors along the CSX line: a siding, a hi-rail truck, and miles of track nobody else walks.

ozet.about.title: Rickhouse Hands
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Rickhouse hands: distillery workers holding a warehouse worth a fortune in barrels, and they know it.

ozet.about.title: Warehouse Night Shift
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Warehouse night shift: the crew that was on the floor when it happened and never went home. Awake all night.

ozet.about.title: Pharmacy Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Pharmacy survivors: the pharmacist, a technician and the stock room, which everyone in the county wants.

ozet.about.title: Postal Holdouts
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Postal holdouts: carriers who know every house on the route and which ones are still answering.

ozet.about.title: Bell Household
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: The Bell household, Riverside: a family in its own house with the doors barred and the shotgun by the stairs.

ozet.about.title: Freeman Porch
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Freeman Porch: a Louisville row house, three generations, and a porch nobody steps onto uninvited.

ozet.about.title: Hensley Orchard
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Hensley Orchard on the Fallas Lake edge: apples, a cider press, and a family that will trade fruit for ammunition.

ozet.about.title: Mercer Auto
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Mercer Auto: a Muldraugh garage family that keeps the shop, fixes what rolls in, and sleeps upstairs.

ozet.about.title: Ortiz Kitchen
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Ortiz Kitchen: a Louisville restaurant family living over the shop, feeding the block from what is left in the walk-in.

ozet.about.title: Nguyen Tailors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Nguyen Tailors: a small Louisville shop, a family behind the shutters, and a very good eye for who is at the door.

ozet.about.title: Bauer Dairy
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Bauer Dairy near Ekron: German farm stock, a herd to keep alive and a fence line they walk twice a day.

ozet.about.title: Walker Duplex
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: The Walker duplex, West Point: two families who knocked the wall through and share one door.

ozet.about.title: Price Motor Court
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Price Motor Court: the family that ran the roadside motel and still rents rooms, for the right trade.

ozet.about.title: Sutter Hardware
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Sutter Hardware, Rosewood: nails, chain, tools and a family that sleeps in the stock room with a shotgun.

ozet.about.title: Lawson Cousins
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: The Lawson cousins in a March Ridge house: four of them, related by marriage and by what they did to keep it.

ozet.about.title: Turner Homestead
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Turner Homestead outside Brandenburg: a smallholding, a well, and a family that has never needed the town.

ozet.about.title: Stranded Commuter
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A stranded commuter in a suit, still carrying the briefcase, walking home from a car that will not start.

ozet.about.title: Lost Hiker
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A lost hiker on the trails who has not seen a road in days and does not know what happened to the towns.

ozet.about.title: Night-Shift Nurse
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A night-shift nurse who walked off the ward with her kit and has been walking since.

ozet.about.title: Retired Neighbour
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A retired neighbour who is not leaving the house, thank you, and has the revolver from the bedside drawer.

ozet.about.title: Stranded Courier
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A stranded courier with a satchel of somebody else's mail and a bicycle helmet, working the roads.

ozet.about.title: Roadside Mechanic
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A roadside mechanic under somebody's bonnet, with a toolbox and no intention of leaving the car.

ozet.about.title: Married Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A married couple who left the house together and have not been apart since.

ozet.about.title: Adult Siblings
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Adult siblings working the neighbourhood house by house, arguing the whole way.

ozet.about.title: Co-Workers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Two co-workers who were on shift together and are still on shift, in a way.

ozet.about.title: Fishing Partners
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Fishing partners at a cabin on the bank, living off the river and a deer rifle.

ozet.about.title: Motel Travellers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Two travellers from a motel room on 31W, out of state, out of gas and out of ideas.

ozet.about.title: Apartment Watch
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Apartment watch: one Louisville block that organised, floor by floor, with a rota on the stairwell door.

ozet.about.title: Trailer Neighbours
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Trailer neighbours at the other end of the Muldraugh park: not Napiers, and they want that understood.

ozet.about.title: Diner Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Diner survivors: the cook, the waitress and the regulars who were there when it started, still there.

ozet.about.title: Church Volunteers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Church volunteers running a shelter in a church that is not Prather's, and glad of the difference.

ozet.about.title: Refugee Walkers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Refugee walkers: a column out of Louisville coming down 31W on foot, carrying everything, going anywhere.

ozet.about.title: Napier Collectors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Napier Collectors: the Napier cousins who went from taking the trailer row to taking everything on the roads around it.

ozet.about.title: Knob Stalkers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Knob Stalkers: hunters who work the farm edges at night with scoped rifles and never show themselves twice.

ozet.about.title: Bone Raiders
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Bone Raiders: the far camp, armoured in bone and hide, come down from the knobs when the food runs out.

ozet.about.title: Cinder Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Cinder Crew: burned out of the industrial yards and black with it. Masks, aprons, leather, and a grudge against everything standing.

ozet.about.title: Scrapyard Reavers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Scrapyard Reavers: a taken workshop, tire and plate armour, sawblade axes. They are slow, and they do not stop.

ozet.about.title: False Checkpoint Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: False Checkpoint Crew: stolen uniforms and a real barrier on a side road. They wave you closer, then they take the car.

ozet.about.title: County Road Militia
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: County Road Militia: farmers and veterans who put a gate on the crossroads and answer to the families behind it.

ozet.about.title: Convoy Predators
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Convoy Predators: the late road crews with body armour, helmets and a captured rifle, hunting the routes between shelters.

ozet.about.title: 5th SFG (Airborne) - Isolated Detachment
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: U.S. Army Special Forces, an isolated A-team of the 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne) from Fort Campbell, on one late mission that has nothing to do with the county. Aim of ten; do not.

ozet.about.title: Delta Force - Isolated Team
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Delta Force, an isolated team long after anyone expected one. Nobody knows what they are here for. Aim of ten.

ozet.about.title: Office Workers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Office staff who walked out of the building on the first morning in their good shoes and name tags. Nobody has told them where to go.

ozet.about.title: Lost Tourist
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A tourist from out of state who pulled off 31W to see Fort Knox and got lost when the rental car broke down.

ozet.about.title: Teen Looking for Parents
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A teenager going house to house looking for Mom and Dad and calling for them at every door.

ozet.about.title: Stuck Trucker
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A long-haul driver whose rig went off the interstate ramp. Still waiting for a tow and calling dispatch on the CB.

ozet.about.title: Hitchhiker
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A hitchhiker on the shoulder of 31W holding a cardboard sign that says NASHVILLE. Rides have been slow.

ozet.about.title: Hired Hand
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A hired hand who stayed on after the family that owns the farm drove off. Still feeding the stock and waiting to get paid.

ozet.about.title: College Student
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A college kid walking home from Louisville to the family place in the county, sleeping in barns and living on vending machine snacks.

ozet.about.title: Old Veteran
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: A Vietnam vet who lives alone at the end of a gravel road and has no use for visitors.

ozet.about.title: Otter Creek Trappers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Two trappers who run their lines along Otter Creek and sell the hides. They know the woods and do not care for company.

ozet.about.title: Mattingly House
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: Three generations of Mattinglys in one house in Irvington. The downstairs windows are boarded and somebody is always awake.

ozet.about.title: Skaggs Farm
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: A tobacco farm outside Echo Creek with a smokehouse full of hams. The Skaggs family keeps count of everybody who comes up the lane.

ozet.about.title: Hornback House
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: A Valley Station family laid off from the plant in the spring. They have been living off the canned goods in the basement since.

ozet.about.title: Pruitt Family
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Families
ozet.about.blurb: The Pruitts left Louisville in the station wagon on the second day and have lived out of it since. They are low on gas and have nowhere to go.

ozet.about.title: Roadside Pickers
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Opportunists working the roads in the first weeks: they strip the houses and cars nobody came back for, tell strangers to keep walking, and take what an outnumbered one is carrying.

ozet.about.title: Knox First Responders
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Relief and Utilities
ozet.about.blurb: Knox First Responders: deputies, firefighters and paramedics who stopped waiting for a dispatcher and started working together. A badge or a helmet on each of them; the rest is whatever still fits.

ozet.about.title: Rolling Fork Settlement
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Rolling Fork Settlement: families, strays and two veterans who pooled what they had behind one fence. They grow, trade and take in people who work, and they want to see your hands first.

ozet.about.title: Long Road Survivors
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Lone Survivors and Households
ozet.about.blurb: Long Road Survivors: people still on the move a month in, in tarp, hide and patched denim, carrying what they could make. Most of them only want to pass.

ozet.about.title: Louisville Transit Strike Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: Louisville Transit Strike Crew: bus drivers and shop mechanics who walked out the week before and now drive one bus south together. They carry wrenches and union cards, and they want a road, not a fight.

ozet.about.title: 100th Division (IT) Reservists - Fort Knox
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Military
ozet.about.blurb: Fort Knox Reservists: weekend soldiers of the 100th Division (Institutional Training) who reported to a post that was already gone. Worn fatigues under civilian coats, a few rifles, and orders nobody left alive can confirm.

ozet.about.title: Salt River Ferrymen
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Survivors
ozet.about.blurb: Salt River Ferrymen: a johnboat crew moving people over the river for fuel or tinned food. They hold the landing, and they wave you off before they let you near the water.

ozet.about.title: Meade County Moonshine Co-op
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Local Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Meade County Moonshine Co-op: stills in the hollows, a fuel trade on the side. They will sell to anyone with something to swap and remember anyone who tries to take it.

ozet.about.title: Sawmill Hands
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Workers
ozet.about.blurb: Sawmill Hands: a logging crew off the Muldraugh cut, felling axes and bats, boots planted. They work in pairs, circle what they cannot take head on, and give a stranger one loud chance to turn round.

ozet.about.title: Knox Commonwealth
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Neighbours, farmers and former responders sharing a council and a watch. They ask to see your hands, not your badge.

ozet.about.title: Ridge Militia League
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Farm households taking turns on the valley roads. Travellers can pass; stealing from a farm is another matter.

ozet.about.title: Valley Caravan League
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Drivers, traders and guards carrying supplies between settlements. Their markets need a clear road and somebody watching it.

ozet.about.title: Ekron Farm Co-op
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Several farms pooling seed, tools and a night watch. There is work for strangers who can put a weapon down.

ozet.about.title: Riverside Ferry Union
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Dock hands and river families keeping their landing supplied. They trade fish and repairs, and watch the bank after dark.

ozet.about.title: Mount Hope Fellowship
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: A kitchen, a schoolroom and a gate watch run by families who took each other in. Help is welcome; trouble stays outside.

ozet.about.title: Foundry Works Collective
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Mechanics and metalworkers keeping a salvage yard running. They will repair what they can if you bring something worth trading.

ozet.about.title: Hollow Compact
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Hollow families sharing hunting ground and stores. They prefer an agreed meeting place to strangers walking into camp.

ozet.about.title: Clinic Circle
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Carers and volunteers running small clinics with whatever they can find. A guarded door buys the patients some peace.

ozet.about.title: Redline Reavers
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: A highway crew living off stolen fuel and other people's convoys. If they block the road, it is not a rescue.

ozet.about.title: The Tithe
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Armed collectors who call robbery a contribution. They demand a share before they shoot, and remember a refusal.

ozet.about.title: Night Shift
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: Raiders who travel after dark and return with food, fuel and somebody else's tools. Their lookout listens before the crew moves.

ozet.about.title: Iron Choir
ozet.about.heading: Survivor Federations and Late Crews
ozet.about.blurb: A long-haul warband with a watch roster and a stockpile. They take settlements seriously enough to plan an attack.

ozet.about.title: Neighbours
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: People from the streets around you who knock because the lights went out or the radio went quiet. They only ever walk up to your door.

ozet.about.title: Drifters
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Hitchhikers, walkers and people with a bag and no destination. They turn up at a door once and move on.

ozet.about.title: Family Folk
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Parents, grandparents, aunts and uncles from the farms and houses nearby, come to ask after your household.

ozet.about.title: Laid-off Workers
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Plant hands and drivers who lost the job before the world did. They know the roads and carry nothing worth taking.

ozet.about.title: Churchfolk
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Pastors, deacons, choir women and congregation members making rounds to see who is left.

ozet.about.title: Medical Folk
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Aides, nurses and the odd country doctor who walk the roads with a bag, offering what little they have.

ozet.about.title: Tradespeople
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Carpenters, linemen, painters and the barber. People whose hands are good for something, calling to trade a favour.

ozet.about.title: Elders
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Old couples, widowers and retired teachers who stayed put and come out slowly, mostly to talk.

ozet.about.title: Young Adults
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: College kids sent home, grocery clerks and musicians in their twenties. Adults every one, a little too curious for their own good.

ozet.about.title: Ex-Service
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Vietnam and Gulf veterans, a guardsman and a deputy, all out of uniform. They are civilians who remember what a checkpoint is.

ozet.about.title: Rough but Harmless
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: Gentle bikers, tattooed drifters and hard-living regulars who look worse than they are. Nothing in their hands.

ozet.about.title: Outsiders
ozet.about.heading: Visitors
ozet.about.blurb: People who were not from here: shop families, farm labourers, tourists, and the ones with a theory about everything.

ozet.about.title: Slackwater Rats
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Bank-side scavengers off the Ohio shore: rubber boots, fishing hats and yellow oilskins. They work the landings at dusk, take what the water leaves and are gone before the lights come on.

ozet.about.title: Black Lung Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Out-of-work miners from the coalfield counties, walking the county with lamp helmets and dust masks over soot-dark faces. They dig in, hold a hill and fight like they are still underground.

ozet.about.title: Breaker Nine Convoy
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Independent truckers who kept hauling and learned that the road pays better when you stop the other man's load. Hi-vis vests, mirror shades and a CB on every dash: they talk over the air, then block the lane.

ozet.about.title: Longshot Crew
ozet.about.heading: 1993 / Late Factions
ozet.about.blurb: Grooms, tipsters and exercise riders from the racetrack barns who ran out of purse money. They wear jockey helmets and riding boots, work the farm lanes by day and bolt for the next gate the moment the odds turn.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetDifficulty_to.en:
Light: 50 damage, 80 health, raids day 60. Only default-valued options change; density is separate. Reload for full effect. Hostile cap affects new admissions only.
Default Standard (2).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CombatReactionDelay.en: Time to raise, aim and start firing, and to look for a new combat target. Default 75%% shortens these delays by one quarter. 100%% restores the previous timing. Lower is faster. Weapon fire rate, reload time and warnings keep their own timings.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ProfessionAffectsAt.en:
Lets your profession affect how NPCs treat you, including Creator rules. Off: profession has no attitude effect; faction and folder relations still apply.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_tooltip.en:
Normal: 200 survivors, 45 resident sites, 6 outposts. Raids scale too. Only default-valued options change; group caps update live, others need reload. Stress test unsupported; may lag.
Default Normal (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RealisticOutbreak_t.en:
Adds extra activity for the first 3 game days and a National Guard checkpoint north of West Point. After 72 hours, road police, army and the checkpoint disappear.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PersistentSquadCap_.en:
Limits outpost garrisons and persistent crews kept after restart. Distant roaming groups and starting building residents have separate limits. Lowering it affects the next save.
Default 45.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostTaskSquadCap.en:
Caps simultaneous patrol, scavenging and hunting teams from each outpost. At 0, none are sent. Teams last for the session; the outpost stays saved.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Party_LoneWeight_to.en:
Sets the relative frequency of natural 1-3-person parties compared with larger groups. Higher means more small parties; faction-specific rules take priority.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Party_GroupWeight_t.en:
Sets the relative frequency of natural groups of 4 or more compared with small parties. Equal weights give both sizes equal selection weight.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Offline_FoundGapHou.en:
Sets the minimum time between new distant roaming groups. Existing groups stay; the world group limit and local quiet periods still apply.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Enabled_toolti.en:
Enables automatic raids: a radio warning, scouts arriving unseen, then a buildup before the attack. The earliest raid day still applies. Admins can force raids.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_MinDay_tooltip.en:
Automatic raids cannot begin before the world reaches this age. For example, 60 prevents them during the first 60 game days.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_CooldownDays_t.en:
Sets the minimum time between automatic full-scale raids. For example, 14 requires at least two game weeks between raids.
Default 21.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Chance_tooltip.en:
Chance for scouts to begin a raid buildup on each check. Set 0 to stop automatic raids; cooldown and earliest-day limits still apply.
Default 0.01.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_CheckMinutes_t.en: How often the raid director checks automatic eligibility.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Waves_tooltip.en:
Sets the number of attacking waves in a raid. The total attacker limit still applies, so extra waves do not bypass that limit.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_GroupSize_tool.en:
Sets the requested attackers in each wave. The total raid limit and other spawn limits can reduce the actual number.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_MaxAttackers_t.en:
Caps attackers across all automatic raid waves, spread evenly among the waves. Earlier scouts do not count. Admin-forced raids ignore this limit.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_WarningHours_t.en:
Sets the warning-to-scout delay; the raid follows its buildup. 0 sends scouts immediately. Scouts and raiders walk in from 40-50 tiles away, unseen and away from player bases.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_WaveDelayMinut.en: Paces reinforcement waves after the initial warning.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Helicopter_too.en:
Allows all A-Life helicopters: raid and backup arrivals, night searchlights and flyovers. Off: none of these helicopters fly.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_SirenAircraftS.en:
Controls opening sirens, jets and raid aircraft sounds. Helicopter raid arrivals also need the helicopter option switched on.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_ScoutBuildupHo.en: Wait this long after scouts successfully arrive before a raid can start.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_ScoutLifetimeH.en: An expired scout report cannot authorize a raid; new scouts must be sent.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_ScoutSize_tool.en:
Sets how many enemy scouts arrive before an automatic full-scale raid. They are separate from the raid's total attacker limit.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_Chance_tool.en:
Sets the chance that an allowed backup call succeeds. For example, 50 gives each permitted call a one-in-two chance of an answer.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_CooldownHou.en: Gap between successful backup calls (game hours)

Sets the minimum wait between successful backup calls by the same group. For example, 6 means it must wait a quarter of a game day.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_GroupSize_t.en:
Sets backup size only when the calling NPC or its faction has no size of its own. It does not replace sizes chosen in their profiles.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_MaxCalls_to.en:
Limits how many reinforcement requests one group may make, preventing repeated backup calls without end.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_SpotlightCh.en:
Sets the chance of a searchlight call from an NPC authorized to request helicopter support. Ground-only callers cannot request it.
Default 12.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_SpotlightSe.en:
Sets how long a requested searchlight flight lasts before the helicopter leaves.
Default 180.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_HelicopterS.en:
Sets how long the support helicopter's flyover effects last. This does not set how long ground reinforcements stay.
Default 35.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Helicopter_Spotligh.en:
Allows moving searchlights at night or in low light. They can reveal people outdoors; cover and buildings hide them. Off disables only the searchlight.
Default on.

Sets the radius of the lit area. A larger beam covers more ground and makes it easier to be caught in the light.
Default 11.

Sets how strongly the helicopter searchlight illuminates the ground.
Default 100.

Sets the minimum time between searchlight flights anywhere in the world. Shorter intervals allow more flights; the call chance still applies.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Residents_ClearCorp.en:
Residents slowly carry zombie corpses out of loaded buildings to reduce corpse sickness. Never removes player or NPC corpses, or corpses in claimed player safehouses.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenge_BuildingRa.en:
Sets how far scavengers look for a nearby building. Higher values widen the search but increase the work needed to find one.
Default 27.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenge_CarryLimit.en:
Scavengers return to their camp or base depot after collecting this many items. For example, 4 sends them home with four collected items.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenge_ReturnAfte.en:
Scavengers bring supplies home after searching this many buildings. For example, 3 allows three building searches before returning.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ALifeEnabled_toolti.en:
Off prevents hostile factions, automatic raids and new outposts. Friendly, neutral and cautious survivors can still appear.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcNight_tooltip.en:
Flashlights: NPCs see 12 tiles in darkness, or 20 when their light reaches you. Night vision: they can see at night, but you must supply goggles yourself.
Default Flashlights (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NightActivity_toolt.en:
How many groups keep travelling and working at night. No risks makes everyone shelter; Risk takers keeps most groups active.
Default Moderate chance (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineSquadCap_too.en:
Saved roaming groups return up to this rate-scaled limit after restart; at 0 or in Local only, the saved-crew cap applies. Lowering stops new groups; extras keep moving until reload.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineTickSeconds_.en:
Sets how often distant roaming groups move and make decisions. Longer intervals mean fewer updates.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineTravelTilesP.en: How far an offline squad walks in one in-game hour. Default 150, a walking pace at the default day length; towns are 1700-3400 tiles apart.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineRevenge_tool.en:
Groups that lose members to you and escape can return for revenge two to three game days later, bringing backup.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsEnabled_too.en:
Lets fortified stations, occupied houses and forest camps appear over time, with garrisons that remain at their site.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsMaxSites_to.en:
Limits how many outposts may exist at once across the map. At 0, outposts are disabled.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsPerCity_too.en:
Limits how many fortified-building outposts each town may hold. Outdoor camps have a separate limit.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsInterval_to.en:
Time between chances to found an outpost. Sleep and fast-forward count. If the game clock stops, checks use this many real minutes instead.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsChance_tool.en:
Chance that an outpost check founds a new site, if a suitable location is available.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsBuildRadius.en:
Normal outposts start within this distance, at least 40 tiles from players. Fixed checkpoints may start up to 200 tiles away; all need loaded ground.
Default 120.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsStreamHold.en: Outpost building pause after travel (real seconds)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsStreamHold_.en:
Pauses multiplayer wall and structure work until players stop crossing map sections. At least 5 seconds protects loading clients; new joins keep a separate 30-second pause.
Default 5.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsStructureLo.en:
Share of destroyed or burned walls, doors, windows and fences that causes an outpost to be removed. At 0, this damage-based removal is disabled.
Default 40.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsSpawnRadius.en: Distance that brings outpost guards in (tiles)

A built outpost receives its garrison when a player comes within this distance.
Default 90.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SupportEnabled_tool.en:
Groups in contact may request backup, with limited calls, a cooldown and a chance of no answer.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PopulationRate_tool.en:
Scales the chance of natural faction encounters. At 50, these checks have half their normal chance of bringing a group.
Default 150.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupScale_tooltip.en:
Scales the number of NPCs in naturally appearing groups. At 100, groups keep their original sizes. Faction size limits still apply.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SimulationRadius_to.en:
Sets how close saved NPCs must be to a player before they appear as physical characters. Larger distances keep more nearby NPCs active.
Default 90.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MaxHostiles_tooltip.en:
Stops new roaming crews at this living-NPC count, including peaceful survivors. It is not the county population; existing crews stay.
Default 12.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterChance_too.en:
Sets the chance of a group on each natural encounter check. Both the game-hour faction checks and game-minute encounter checks use it.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterInterval_t.en:
Sets the time between natural faction encounter checks. A check can fail; this is not a guaranteed time between meetings.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SafehouseMargin_too.en:
Extra no-spawn distance around claimed multiplayer safehouses. At 8, new NPCs cannot spawn within eight extra tiles of the claim.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Warfare_tooltip.en:
Allows hostile NPC factions to fight each other.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Retreat_tooltip.en:
Allows wounded hostile NPCs to retreat from a fight.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NPCsReanimate_toolt.en:
NPCs infected by zombie bites or attacks can rise in their own clothes. The game's Transmission, Mortality and Reanimate settings still apply.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TurningDelay_toolti.en:
Infected NPC corpses wait before rising, giving you time to right-click and put them down. Off: they rise immediately. The wait advances only while the body is loaded.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TurningDelayMin_too.en:
Sets the shortest wait before an infected NPC corpse rises. For example, 30 means at least half a minute while the body is loaded.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TurningDelayMax_too.en:
Sets the longest wait before an infected NPC corpse rises. For example, 120 allows up to two minutes while the body is loaded.
Default 90.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenging_tooltip.en:
Allows hostile looters to take nearby supplies.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Investigate_tooltip.en:
Hostile NPCs may walk toward gunfire, shouts and other signs of activity they notice.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Regroup_tooltip.en: Members that fall behind close back up on their group instead of drifting.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupMarch_tooltip.en: Groups travel together in formation rather than as separate walkers.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CloseDoors_tooltip.en:
Outside combat, the last group member closes doors the group opened. Player-opened doors and occupied doorways stay untouched; no locks are changed.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WeaponDrops_tooltip.en:
Allows eligible NPC guns and melee weapons to remain on their bodies for looting. The weapon drop chance still applies.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DropsWeaponChance_t.en:
Per NPC profile uses each NPC's own chance times the NPC loot percent. Another choice sets one chance for all weapons and ignores that percent; needs NPC weapon drops.
Default Per NPC profile (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DropsWeaponConditio.en:
Sets dropped weapon condition, not NPC combat strength. Per NPC profile keeps its rating and early-game wear curve; Broken needs repairs before use.
Default Per NPC profile (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WeaponJamming_toolt.en:
Allows NPC firearms other than revolvers to jam: the gun clicks instead of firing, then the NPC racks it clear.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WeaponJamChance_too.en: Base chance per trigger pull for a non-revolver NPC firearm to jam. Zero disables jams even if the feature is enabled.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BreachStrength_tool.en: How hard NPCs work a door, a window or a barricade when they break in. 100 is the tested default: a window takes three swings, a plank four, a plain door about half a minute, and only one man swings while the rest cover him. Lower it and they take longer; raise it and they come through faster.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MultiHit_tooltip.en: A two-handed swing by an NPC carries into a second zombie standing in the arc, at three quarters of the blow. Zombies only, never people. Off by default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BulletPenetration_t.en: A round an NPC puts into a zombie goes on into the zombie standing right behind it (up to three squares). Zombies only, never people; better against a horde. Off by default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PopulateOnStart_too.en:
Marks 10, 20 or 35 percent of suitable buildings once per world. Residents appear when approached and are saved. Realistic outbreak does not enable this.
Default Off (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TownWelcomeEnabled_.en:
Adds small local groups, such as a family or rescue crew, when a new character starts in town. Reloading or rejoining does not add more.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TownWelcomeGroups_t.en:
How many welcome groups each new character gets, and how many can be alive in one town at once, even when several players start there.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TownWelcomeFirstDay.en:
On allows a character's town welcome group only during their first game day. Off extends the window to their first game week.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PopulateMax_tooltip.en:
Limits buildings selected for starting residents across the whole map. Selection happens once per world; stations, firehouses and clinics take priority.
Default 45.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CensusSize_tooltip.en:
Sets the finite survivor pool when the world starts. Natural groups and reinforcements draw from it; deaths reduce it. Slow arrivals replace losses. Admin spawns do not count.
Default 200.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CensusArrivalsEarly.en:
Sets how many newcomers can replace dead survivors each game week early in the outbreak. If nobody has died, nobody arrives.
Default 7.0.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CensusArrivalsLate_.en:
Sets the replacement arrival rate after the early period. Arrivals gradually fall from the early rate to this one; they only replace losses.
Default 1.0.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CensusArrivalsFadeD.en:
Sets how long the weekly arrival rate takes to fall from the early value to the later value.
Default 28.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CensusClearedDays_t.en:
Keeps a camp, outpost or inhabited building empty after all its residents die. Once this period ends, rare newcomers may settle there if resettlement is enabled.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CensusResettle_tool.en:
Allows newcomers to settle cleared sites after their vacancy period, at most one site per four arrivals. Off keeps cleared sites empty for the rest of the game.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Search_tooltip.en: NPCs walk to where a target was last seen and sweep the area before giving up.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SearchShout_tooltip.en: Shouting draws every NPC within earshot toward you.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SearchCallout_toolt.en: An NPC that spots something tells its group where, once. Not a live feed.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_tooltip.en:
When not fighting, NPCs search areas with signs that survivors are nearby, such as barricades or a running generator.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesVehicles_toolt.en:
Running or hotwired vehicles attract NPC searches in the surrounding area.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesBarricades_too.en:
Planks on doors and windows make NPCs treat a building as occupied and worth investigating.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesPlayerBuilt_to.en:
Player-built walls, gates and fences make NPCs treat a place as occupied and worth investigating.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesPower_tooltip.en:
A running generator gives NPCs a strong sign that someone lives nearby, attracting investigation.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesWeight_tooltip.en:
Scales how readily NPCs investigate survivor traces. Higher values let weaker evidence draw a search; lower values require stronger evidence.
Default 1.0.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Voice_tooltip.en:
Enables recorded speech where available. Off keeps conversations as text; pain and death sounds are separate.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ShowAdminTools.en: Show admin tools in the right-click menu

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ShowAdminTools_tool.en:
The admin console, spawn panel, encounter list, outpost builder and raid setup in the right-click menu. Players also need Diagnostics ticked in Options. Turn this off for a clean right-click menu; the Creator (Insert key) and world status (Home key) stay on their keys and the pause menu. Admins on a server are unaffected.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CleanupRespawnAfter.en: Let A-Life spawn again after a completed cleanup

After an admin has run CLEANUP A-LIFE to the end, the mod stays inert in that world so it can be removed safely. Turn this on only if you want the mod to spawn people and outposts again in a cleaned world.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Peek_Enabled_toolti.en:
Adds a right-click peephole view on closed doors. Each player can also turn it off in their own mod options.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Peek_NoticeChancePe.en: Chance of being heard while peeking (percent)

Every few seconds, an NPC within two tiles of the door may hear you peeking and speak. They cannot see you through the peephole. At 0, peeking is never heard.
Default 5.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_MysteryMode_to.en:
Hides faction, rank, mood and standing in the talk window. Shows only a name you have learned and held items. Off restores the full heading.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.VehicleDamage_toolt.en:
Moving vehicles hurt NPCs they hit, with damage based on speed. Off: collisions do no NPC damage. Intact car windows still protect you from NPC attacks either way.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NonPvpZoneShield_to.en:
On: NPCs do not start fights in non-PvP zones, but still retaliate against an attacker. Off: NPCs may attack there. Safehouses protect you either way.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AimDifficulty_toolt.en:
Higher choices make NPC gunfire more accurate against players. Medium keeps their own aiming skill; zombie accuracy is separate.
Default Medium (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AimPlayerPercent_to.en: Global multiplier on how often NPC gunfire hits players, applied on top of the NPC aim setting and each character's own accuracy. 100 is unchanged. NPCs also aim worse in the first seconds of a fight, at long range and against a moving target.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcDamagePercent_to.en:
Scales NPC melee and gun damage to players. At 50, each hit deals half the original damage; 100 is the original amount.
Default 72.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ExtraWoundPercent_t.en: Optional extra overall-health loss added on top of a hit, on top of the damage option above. 0 means no extra damage, so the 60%% option is exactly 60%% of the original hit. Default 0.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcHealthPercent_to.en:
Scales each survivor's original health. At 80, they have four-fifths of their usual health; profession differences still apply.
Default 98.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcDamageTakenPerce.en: How hard bullets, melee hits, shoves and zombie bites land on NPCs, on top of the NPC maximum health setting. At 100 guns, shoves and bites cost what they used to, 130 is 30%% more. Melee hits are priced so that the defaults keep the old number of swings. This is the damage NPCs receive, not what they deal to players (see NPC damage output). Default 130.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcRegenPercent_too.en: How fast a resting NPC recovers health. 100 is the original 1.5%% of maximum health per game hour, 50 is half of that. Only an NPC that has been out of the fight for two minutes and has no open wound recovers. 0 turns recovery off. Default 50.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcHealthLegacy_too.en: Switches the NPC health rebalance off: original maximum health, original hits needed to put an NPC down, original bleeding and regeneration. Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RoomSweep_tooltip.en: NPCs carrying a weapon walk into buildings slowly with the weapon raised, pause at doorways and corners and look over the room before moving on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AimZombiePercent_to.en: Scales how often NPC gunfire hits a ZOMBIE. 100 is unchanged; raise it if crews look helpless against a horde. Does not affect their aim against you.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Tracers_tooltip.en:
Shows a visible streak along NPC gunshots. Turning this off does not change muzzle flashes, gunfire sounds or casings.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MuzzleFlash_tooltip.en:
Shows weapon-sized flashes and nearby ground light when NPCs fire. Suppressed weapons do not flash. Gunfire sounds and casings are unchanged.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ShotFxRange_tooltip.en:
Sets how far other players can see an NPC shot's flash and streak and hear its gunshot and casing in multiplayer.
Default 90.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleCover_tooltip.en: Armed NPCs get out of the line of fire to reload, break contact when hurt, and fight from behind walls and corners.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleWithdraw_tool.en: A shooter that is losing breaks contact, runs about a block back, holes up out of sight -- inside a building when there is one -- then comes back in from another side. Ranged only; melee always closes.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleHealing_toolt.en: After a fight, a wounded NPC stops, bandages, and loses the limp and the bleeding.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Wounds_tooltip.en:
Hits cause bruises, fractures, cuts, bullet wounds or bites. Leg wounds slow NPCs, arm wounds spoil aim, and open wounds bleed until bandaged; below 10 percent health, bleed-out is rapid.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryBleed_tooltip.en: How fast an NPC's open wounds bleed: scratches and cuts clot on their own, deep wounds and bullet wounds bleed until bandaged. 0 turns the bleeding off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BluntFracture_toolt.en: Chance that an NPC's hit with a heavy blunt weapon (bat, sledgehammer) breaks the player's arm or leg it lands on. Blunt weapons never cut: a laceration becomes a scratch.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SprintEnabled_toolt.en: Allows sprint windows for melee closing, cover moves, and retreats. Off keeps those moves at a run or walk.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleGunner_toolti.en: A shooter that loses sight of its target dumps the magazine into the last known position, full auto, spraying left and right. Pistols magdump too.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Encounters_tooltip.en:
Allows groups such as patrols, scavengers and hostile crews to appear near players in suitable map areas.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterRollInterv.en:
Sets the time between random encounter checks, including while sleeping or fast-forwarding. The encounter chance still decides whether a group appears.
Default 120.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DormantTtl_tooltip.en:
Removes inactive NPCs after nobody has approached them for this long. Persistent crews, such as anchored NPCs and garrisons, never expire. At 0, cleanup is disabled.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleBehaviors_too.en: The conduct layer: squad leaders that deploy and rally their group, snipers that keep distance, medics that dress their wounded, ambushers that wait in the dark, stealth killers. Off disables every conduct at once.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleStrafe_toolti.en: Armed NPCs keep the gun on their target, or on where it was last seen, while they walk, back off or sidestep.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WorldMode_tooltip.en:
Full keeps groups travelling beyond players' view. Local only stops new distant groups; existing ones retire on reload. Outposts can still develop in either mode.
Default Full A-Life (offline squads roam the map) (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WorldMode_option1.en: Full A-Life (offline squads roam the map)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WorldMode_option2.en: Local only (groups near players; outposts stay)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateEncounters_tool.en:
Scales the chance of a random group near players without changing check intervals. Low halves the chance; Abundant triples it.
Default Normal (2).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateGroups_tooltip.en:
Scales natural group arrivals and the distant roaming group limit together. Low halves both; Abundant triples them, within their limits.
Default Normal (2).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateSurvivors_toolt.en:
Scales how often friendly, neutral and wary factions are picked compared with hostile ones. Low halves their selection weight; Abundant triples it.
Default Normal (2).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateMetaEvents_tool.en:
Changes distant gunfire, helicopters and other background events. Low halves event limits and doubles the wait between them.
Default Normal (2).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsOutsideCity.en:
Limits outdoor sites such as forest camps, field bases and aid stations, separate from fortified town buildings. At 0, outdoor sites are disabled.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestEnabled_t.en:
Patrols and scouts pause off the road every few hours and after fights to sit, smoke, drink or talk, then resume their route.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestMinMinute.en:
Sets the minimum length of a patrol rest. For example, 30 means each rest lasts at least half a game hour.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestMaxMinute.en:
Sets the maximum length of a patrol rest. For example, 60 limits each rest to one game hour.
Default 45.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestEveryHour.en:
Sets the usual time between a group's planned rests, with some variation. Rest after a fight is separate from this schedule.
Default 3.0.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkEnabled_tooltip.en:
Nearby NPCs answer typed questions, requests, threats and yes-or-no replies. They also speak when you hit them or help them fight.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkSinglePlayerCha.en:
The Toggle chat key opens a small chat line for talking to NPCs in single player. Start a message with ! to shout.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkPresence_toolti.en:
Friendly and neutral NPCs notice you nearby, stop and look when you speak. Passing friends greet you; outlaw groups call out strangers.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkRiskAssessment_.en:
Fresh survivors avoid unprovoked fights, but hostile relations, grudges and self-defence still allow attacks. Veterans and predators ignore this caution.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationRadioName.en:
Radio stories may name players after lasting reputation changes, fighting sprees or surviving raids. Requires personal reputation; never reveals the player's location.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationRadioBadN.en:
Allows radio stories about a player's bad reputation. Off: only neutral or positive mentions are broadcast.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationTracking_.en:
Tracks kills, help and mistreatment, with change notices and character-window scores. Off stops both tracking and display.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationNpcOpinio.en:
Each NPC remembers a separate opinion of each player, shaped by temperament, reputation and deeds toward their group. Shown in conversations. Off disables individual opinions.
Default on.
Opinion changes from deeds (percent of normal)

Scales how deeds change an NPC's opinion. At normal strength, a gift gives about 8 points, a hit loses 20 and killing a groupmate loses 45; others may hear about it.
Default 100.
Influence of NPC opinion (percent of normal)

Scales opinion's effect on prices, replies, invitations, company, deals, greetings, betrayal and orders. At 0, opinion is displayed but has no gameplay effect.
Default 100.
NPC opinion fade (points per game day)

How far each NPC's opinion moves back toward its starting value each day. At 0, the NPC never forgets.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationMode.en: Faction standing from gifts and trades

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationMode_tool.en:
Food gifts and fair trades improve standing with the visitor's faction. Off: these choices do not change faction standing; existing grudges remain.
Default Off (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationDecayPerc.en:
How quickly earned faction standing returns toward zero. At 200, it fades twice as fast; at 0, earned standing stays unchanged.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationResetOnNe.en: Fresh reputation for a new character

New characters reset personal reputation, faction standing and NPC memories, not faction or Creator relations. Off keeps the old values. Reconnecting never resets the same character.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationShowScore.en:
Shows the number beside your reputation level in the character window, notes and radio panel, such as Cutthroat (-62). Off shows only the level name.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationShowOther.en:
The T-menu reputation answer also lists other players' reputation levels on the server. Off shows only your own.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationNpcFightI.en: Hostile credit for killing fighting NPCs

Killing an NPC already in a fight counts as a hostile kill and is not held against you. Off judges each kill by the NPC's attitude toward you.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationDriftPerD.en: Personal reputation fade (points per game day)

Points of personal reputation that drift toward neutral each day. At 0, your earned reputation stays unchanged.
Default 5.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationKillScale.en: Reputation changes from kills and deeds (percent of normal)

Scales personal reputation changes from kills and from deeds (visitors, hosting, gifts, treating, trading). At 0 none count; at 200 they count twice as much.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationGainCapPe.en:
Limits reputation gained from kills each day at full rate; extra hostile kills count at the reduced share below. Deeds get their own limit of 150 percent of this.
Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationOverCapPe.en: Reputation gain beyond the daily limit (percent)

Share of normal gain earned for hostile or criminal kills after the daily limit, with at least 1 point per kill. At 0, no further gain is possible that day.
Default 25.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationHysteresi.en:
Extra points beyond a level boundary needed before your reputation label changes. Higher values reduce frequent label changes.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationKillHosti.en: Reputation gain for a hostile kill (points)

Personal reputation gained for killing an NPC who was hostile toward you.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationKillCrime.en: Reputation gain for a criminal kill (points)

Personal reputation gained for killing an NPC from a criminal faction.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationKillNeutr.en: Reputation loss for a neutral kill (points)

Personal reputation lost for killing a neutral or cautious NPC who meant you no harm.
Default 40.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationKillFrien.en: Reputation loss for a friendly kill (points)

Personal reputation lost for killing an NPC who regarded you as a friend.
Default 80.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ReputationKillSurre.en: Reputation loss for a surrendered kill (points)

Personal reputation lost for killing an NPC who had surrendered.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkGroupMeetings_t.en:
Non-enemy groups within eight tiles may stop and talk, then part or walk together briefly. Off disables meetings; fights, fleeing and player orders always interrupt.
Default Normal (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ChatterEnabled_tool.en:
Calm groups pause to talk, and passing NPCs greet each other or you. Danger interrupts them. Off disables both group chatter and these greetings.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ChatterFrequency_to.en:
How often calm groups start talking. At 200, conversations happen twice as often; at 50, half as often.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ChatterPassingGreet.en:
Chance that an NPC greets you or another NPC while passing. Friendly people greet more, wary people less, enemies never. At 0, passing greetings stop.
Default 70.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ChatterMaxConcurren.en:
Maximum group conversations happening at once. Lower values keep speech easier to follow in crowded places.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RobberyEnabled_tool.en:
Outlaws may rob a lone player instead of shooting: hands up, weapon down, three or four valuables taken, then they leave. Refusal can lead to shooting.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RobberyChance_toolt.en:
Scales how often outlaws choose robbery rather than a fight. 0 means never; 200 means twice the normal rate, not a guaranteed robbery.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersEnabled_toolt.en:
Lets you order NPCs to raise their hands, drop weapons, leave or follow. Obedience depends on fear, faction, weapons and group size.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersChance_toolti.en:
Scales the chance an NPC obeys a spoken order. At 0, nobody obeys; at 200, obedience is twice as likely. Civilians are easier to command than armed factions.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersFailFight.en: Fight chance after a failed hold-up (percent)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersFailFight_too.en:
Chance the target and their group attack after refusing hands-up, drop-weapon or hold-up orders. At 100, they always attack; at 0, they only refuse.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersZombieTiles_t.en:
A surrendering NPC lowers their hands and reacts when a zombie comes within this distance.
Default 4.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersSurrenderSeco.en:
Longest time an NPC keeps their hands up before lowering them and carrying on.
Default 90.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersAdvantage_too.en:
How much weapons, loaded ammo, armour, numbers, distance and clear sight affect obedience. At 0, these advantages do not matter; at 300, they dominate the decision.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersGroupSurrende.en:
When one member surrenders, each groupmate chooses whether to obey, fight or flee after a warning. Off: the whole group always follows the surrendering member.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OrdersCarefulMinute.en:
Robbed NPCs flee, then remember you as dangerous and keep their distance for this long. At 0, this caution is not remembered.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkGreetOnOpen_too.en:
Opening a calm NPC's talk menu makes them stop, face you and greet you before choices appear. Fighting or frightened NPCs are not interrupted.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkAntiSpam_toolti.en:
NPCs remember repeated questions, lose patience and react to your tone. Off: no question memory or opinion changes from words; deeds still count.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkMenuFocus_toolt.en:
Prioritises useful replies, marks asked questions and hides unsuitable choices, such as personal questions for strangers. Requires conversation memory and patience.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkRepeatCooldownM.en:
Within this time, a repeated question gets an already-answered reply and no opinion gain. Personal-life answers stay remembered for a full game day.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkQuestionsPerTal.en:
Base number of questions an NPC will answer. NPCs who like you allow more; those who dislike you allow fewer. After warning that patience is spent, they end the talk.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkRefuseMinutes_t.en:
After ending an overlong or irritating conversation, the NPC refuses to answer and closes the talk window until this time passes.
Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkPersonalAfterTa.en:
Talks needed before family and past-life questions open up, unless the NPC already likes you. Asking too early lowers their opinion.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkOpinionFromTalk.en: Opinion changes from conversation (percent of normal)

Scales how much polite, nosy, rude or kind words change an NPC's opinion. At 0, words do not change opinion; repetition, patience and refusals still work.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkOpinionCapPerCo.en:
Limits opinion gained from words in one talk; losses stop at one and a half times this amount. Twenty quiet game minutes begin a new conversation.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkOpinionCapPerDa.en:
Limits opinion gained from words with each NPC per game day. Losses stop at one and a half times this amount.
Default 12.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkOpinionWordCeil.en:
Conversation cannot raise an NPC's opinion above this score. Beyond it, gifts, healing or fighting beside them must earn further trust.
Default 40.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BodyLootEnabled_too.en:
