After fights, NPCs near players loot bodies when no danger is within 15 tiles, taking supplies and useful gear. Player bodies and former player companions' bodies are left alone.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BodyLootPerMinute.en: Corpse searches per group (per real minute)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BodyLootPerMinute_t.en:
Caps how many bodies one group searches each real minute. For example, 2 prevents it searching more than two corpses in a minute.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RadioKnoxCounty_too.en:
Adds a survivor-run station with scanner traffic, military chatter, calls, stories, jokes and rumors about events in your world.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RadioKnoxFrequency_.en:
Choose an unused frequency; 100000 means 100 MHz. Other channels are never replaced. Restart the server after changes, then open a radio to add the matching preset.
Default 99600.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootRareDropPercent.en:
Only military and special-response crews can drop rare armor, dirty and at 10-40 percent condition. 0 stops these drops. Sledgehammers and crafting components never drop.
Default 5.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootAllowRareFromPr.en:
On: Creator profiles keep their chosen rare gear. Off: custom sledgehammers, crafting heads and heavy armor are replaced with common gear at spawn.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FactionsLegacyRoste.en:
Restores the earlier factions, attitudes and spawn weights instead of the merged roster. Takes effect when the game or server starts.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FunnelEnabled_toolt.en:
Changes factions, gear and aim as the world ages. Emergency services disappear by day 120; survivor and raider groups take over. Off uses fixed faction schedules.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FunnelDayOffset_too.en:
Moves faction progression ahead or back. At +30, a new world uses day-30 factions and gear; -10 delays progression by 10 days.
Default 0.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FunnelLoneSurvivorM.en:
Limits lone survivors and survivor pairs to this many NPCs, even if group-size settings would make their party larger.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FunnelSkillRampPerc.en: How much NPC aim improves as the stages pass, in %% of the built-in ramp (up to +3 aim rating in the last stage). 0%% turns the ramp off, 100%% is the default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AmmoSpawnPercent_to.en:
Scales the ammo an NPC starts with; 100 keeps its profile amount. Each gun retains at least one full load. Infinite-ammo profiles are unchanged.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AmmoReserveLoads_to.en:
Caps starting and collected spare ammo in gun loads of at least 6 rounds. Smaller kits stay smaller; 2 permits two spare loads. 0 removes the cap; infinite-ammo profiles are unchanged.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AmmoBottomless_tool.en:
Chooses which NPC profiles may use infinite ammo. Creator profiles only limits it to profiles you made or edited; stock NPCs can run dry.
Default Creator profiles only (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AmmoHonestDrops_too.en:
On: dropped magazines use only ammo the NPC had left, up to its profile limit. Off: each issued magazine gets a drop roll and can be full even after its rounds were fired.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EarlyLooters_toolti.en:
Scales Roadside Pickers, small looting crews that may warn or rob you. They are common in the first two weeks and gone by week four. At 0, they do not appear.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SeasonalDress_toolt.en:
Adds winter layers, removes heavy layers in summer and adds rainwear in wet weather. Uniforms and profiles with their own seasonal outfits are preserved.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AppearanceVariation.en:
Each new person gets their own hair, hair colour, beard and clothing colours, so crews stop looking cloned. Off keeps the authored look. People already in a save keep theirs.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AppearanceKeepAutho.en:
Share of new people who keep their authored face, so named characters stay recognisable. 0 varies everyone, 100 varies nobody. Needs Varied NPC looks on.
Default 35.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.AppearanceLoadoutVa.en: People whose profile lists several weapons for one slot pick one of them per person. Off always uses the first listed weapon. Profiles with a single weapon are unaffected. Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdEnabled_tooltip.en:
Weather and clothing affect NPC warmth. Prolonged chill can cause coughing, worse aim, slower walking and faster fatigue. Indoors or near a fire, NPCs warm up.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdSeverity_toolti.en: How hard the cold hits NPCs and how big the penalties of a cold are. 0 = NPCs never get chilled. 100 = default and gentle. 300 = harsh winters. Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdChance.en: [Expert] Cold: chance of catching a cold (%% per chilled hour)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdChance_tooltip.en: Per game hour spent badly chilled, the base chance that an NPC comes down with a cold (it grows with how chilled and wet the NPC is). 0 = chills never turn into a cold. Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdSneezeNoise.en: [Expert] Cold: sneezes and coughs make a little noise

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdSneezeNoise_too.en: A sneeze or cough from a sick NPC is a small sound (a few tiles) that nearby zombies can hear. Turn off to keep them silent.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ColdSeekWarmth_tool.en:
Chilled NPCs without orders or danger seek a fire or heated building and wear warmer clothes from their packs. Groups follow their leader to a fire.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.IdleCampWarmHands_t.en:
In cold weather, NPCs sitting beside a lit campfire periodically hold their hands toward it. In warm weather or without a fire, they just sit.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.IdleFishingAnim_too.en:
Shore fishers cast, wait and pull their rods every 20-60 seconds. Off: they continue fishing without the rod animation.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.IdleBenchSeat_toolt.en:
Camp sitters beside a free outdoor bench sit on it instead of the ground. Off: they always sit on the ground.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairTell.en: [Expert] Hostiles warn before the first attack

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairTell_tooltip.en: A hostile NPC never lands its first blow or shot on a player who has not attacked it unless the player had a fair chance to notice: a shouted warning, a door or window heard opening, or the NPC in plain view for the first-contact grace. Fighting back is never delayed.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairGrace_tooltip.en: How long a hostile NPC must have been in your view before it may attack without shouting first.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairWarningLead_too.en: Time between a hostile NPC's warning shout and its first blow or shot.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairEntryLead.en: [Expert] Warning after a door or window is heard (seconds)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairEntryLead_toolt.en: Time between the sound of a hostile NPC opening a door or climbing through a window and its first attack on a player nearby.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairWindowOpen_tool.en: How long an NPC needs to open a closed window before it climbs through. The window can be heard opening.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FairFightMemory_too.en: How long NPCs remember who started a fight with a player. Fighting back inside this time is self-defence, and the NPC that started it does not speak like a victim.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WarningEnabled_tool.en:
Enables warnings for crews set to warn; others attack on sight unless a chance below allows a warning. Off: hostile crews attack on sight. Careful factions keep their own rules.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WarningChance_toolt.en:
Sets the share of normally kill-on-sight crews that warn anyway. Each group rolls once and keeps its result. 0 means none; 100 means all. Raids use their separate chance.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WarningRaidChance_t.en:
Sets the share of raids, assassins, highway ambushers and admin-spawned attackers that warn first. 0 makes all of these crews attack on sight.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WarningHold_tooltip.en:
Limits unanswered warnings, standoffs and hold-ups. A crew waits four fifths of this per warning or demand before the next step. Replies restart the clock, up to four times this limit.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterStandoffs_.en:
Crews that warn may question you, demand a toll or call you outside before fighting. Silence, leaving, a raised gun or betrayal can start a fight. Off: only their attack warning remains.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterSurprise_t.en: How long a hostile crew holds its fire after it discovers a player: time to answer, drop the weapon, raise the hands or act first. Aiming at the crew or attacking it ends the beat at once.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterAnswer_too.en: How long a confronting crew waits for an answer before it asks again ('Will you answer me?'). After the third silence the crew acts: leave, warn or attack, by faction.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterCallout.en: Calls to leave a building (percent of faction habit)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterCallout_to.en:
Scales how often crews call hidden players outside instead of searching; police do this more than raiders. Player bases are always called out first. 0 disables ordinary callouts.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterCalloutTim.en: How long a crew outside a building waits for the player to answer or come out, with repeated calls and a warning shot, before it searches the building or leaves. The time left is shown to the player.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterBetrayal.en: Outlaw flanking during talks (percent of faction habit)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterBetrayal_t.en:
Scales outlaw flanking during talks. A flanker circles while the leader stalls; calling it out or raising a gun makes them back off. 0 disables this betrayal.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterSearch_too.en: How long a crew searches a building where it believes a player is hiding: one man at the door, the rest room by room. Then it gives up and moves on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterLostSight_.en: How long an NPC keeps chasing a player it can no longer see or hear. After that it only knows where he was last seen and searches from there.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterFixBlur_to.en: A hunting, raiding or revenge crew gets ONE tip about where its target is when it sets out, off by up to this many tiles. It never follows the player's live position; it searches and gives up.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterCues_toolt.en:
Stand-offs and hold-ups lean on gestures and distance instead of text over heads: one spoken line per phase (notice, demand, turn, parting), the rest goes to the talk panel, hand signals and nods carry the in-between. Every line is picked so it does not repeat. Off: every line is shouted over the head as before.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FriskScripted_toolt.en:
In a hold-up one crew member, never the speaker if someone else is free, walks up to arm's length and pats you down with an animation and one of three pat-down sounds. The search lasts exactly as long as the sound. If you step away or fight, it stops and the crew reacts. Off: the old instant search.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RevengeMaxWaves_too.en:
Limits revenge groups sent after a player for one grudge. Each is drawn from the original crew's survivors plus at most two reinforcements.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutplayStagger_tool.en:
Your shoves briefly stagger NPCs, and melee hits interrupt their next swing. A staggered NPC cannot finish its attack.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.UniformDecayDay_too.en:
New arrivals from built-in factions mix uniforms with civilian clothes from this day; makeshift armour appears later. At 0, uniforms stay intact. Creator profiles are unchanged.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ArmingPace_tooltip.en:
Sets how quickly built-in civilian groups gain guns over time. At 200, guns spread twice as fast; at 50, half as fast. Police, army and elite units are unaffected.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ArmingShare_tooltip.en:
Scales gun ownership among built-in non-military NPCs. At 0, affected NPCs use melee tools only. Police, army, elite units and Creator profiles are unchanged.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsSurvivorHol.en:
Allows cautious survivor communities to hold outposts alongside hostile crews. They warn strangers away but never send hunting parties. Off leaves only hostile holders.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverEnabled_t.en:
Unvisited scavenged buildings may have fewer valuables and signs of looting. Never changes buildings players entered, player bases, safehouses or outposts.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverStrength.en: Previously scavenged building rate (percent of normal)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverStrength_.en:
Scales the chance that a building is already scavenged. 100 keeps the usual chance, 300 triples it and 0 disables it.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverBaseline_.en:
Sets the base chance before building type and rate scaling. Nearby scavenging adds up to 60 percentage points before those adjustments.
Default 5.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverVisuals_t.en:
Already scavenged buildings may show open doors, broken windows and blood. These signs are placed only while every player is at least 40 tiles away.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverZombieCor.en:
Already scavenged buildings may contain one or two dead zombies.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PickedOverFactionCo.en:
A building may rarely contain a dead member of the group that scavenged the area, wearing that group's clothes and carrying its gear.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.WarDeadEnabled_tool.en:
NPCs killed in battles away from players leave dressed bodies at the battle site. Bodies are placed while players are 40-110 tiles away and forgotten after 14 game days.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BoardingStaged_tool.en:
Outposts start with one or two ground-floor planks, adding more every four game days while players stay over 40 tiles away. Upstairs gets sheets; metal bars stay unchanged.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PanicFirstDays_tool.en:
Civilians, families and workers flee zombies, flinch at loud events and spread fear early in the outbreak. Soldiers, police and criminals stay steadier. Requires Civilian fear of zombies.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PanicStrength_toolt.en: 100%% is the standard curve: full fright on days 0 and 1, then easing off. Lower values make survivors calmer, higher values keep them frightened longer. 0 turns the panic off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PanicLengthDays_too.en:
Stretches or shortens the early-outbreak panic curve. Fright is strongest at the start and nearly gone by this many days after the outbreak.
Default 12.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PanicContagion_tool.en: A frightened survivor makes the people around them more frightened for 30 to 60 seconds: their own group first, strangers within about 12 tiles less. Soldiers and police nearby calm them down. Off keeps every survivor's fright separate.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleFear_tooltip.en:
Civilians, families and workers avoid distant zombies and flee crowds for at least 30 seconds, fighting if cornered. Soldiers, police, criminals and hardened members stay steadier.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FearDays_tooltip.en: Civilians start out at full fear and steady over this many days, down to the lingering fear below. 0 starts them at the lingering fear.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FearLevel_tooltip.en: How many zombies it takes before civilians break and run.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FearLingering_toolt.en: How much of their fear civilians keep once they have steadied. At 50 it takes a crowd about 1.6 times the size to make them run. 0 means they stop running from zombies altogether after the days above.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunFearEnabled_tool.en:
Poorly armed NPCs back away from a player or hostile aiming or raising a firearm. The Creator determines which factions and members have this fear.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunFearPercent_tool.en: Chance that an NPC panics when a gun is aimed at it. Rolled once per NPC and player, so the same NPC always reacts the same way to the same player. A gun that is raised but not pointed at it counts half. Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunFearRunDistance_.en: How far, in tiles, a frightened NPC runs from the gun on each leg. It heads for cover that breaks line of sight and keeps going until the gun has been out of sight for a few seconds. Default 35.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunFearRunSpeed_too.en: How fast a frightened NPC runs away. A flight may use all of its stamina and slows down only when it is empty.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunFearReactDelay_t.en: How long an NPC freezes and stares at the gun before it starts to run. 0 runs at once. Default 400.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeFootwork_toolt.en: In melee, NPCs step back while swinging when zombies press or outnumber them, and step in when a lone zombie is within reach or backing off. Decided each swing from the zombies' positions and facing.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeKiteCrowd.en: [Expert] Zombies that make an NPC step back

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeKiteCrowd_tool.en: How many zombies facing an NPC within the step-back radius it takes before the NPC steps back between swings. 0 turns stepping back off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeKiteTiles_tool.en: How far around an NPC zombies are counted for melee footwork.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeStepBack_toolt.en: How far an NPC steps back between swings. It never steps out of weapon reach. 16 is 1.6 tiles.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeStepIn_tooltip.en: How far an NPC steps toward a lone zombie that is in reach or backing off. 11 is 1.1 tiles.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieStunMs.en: [Expert] Zombie stun after an NPC melee hit (milliseconds)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieStunMs_toolti.en: A zombie an NPC has just struck with a melee weapon cannot start or finish a bite and stops chasing for this long, so a fighter who keeps swinging is not bitten by the zombie in front of him. 0 turns the stun off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewEnabled_to.en: Master switch. On: the Sawmill Hands crew can spawn and the five melee modules work. Off: the faction is hidden from spawning, the Creator and the debug spawner, and every melee module is inert.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewFootwork_t.en: Sidestep between swings, back off when zombies press in, step back in afterwards. Tuned for pairs and groups.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewFlank_tool.en: In a melee group one member engages and the others circle round to the far side of the target.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewBreach_too.en: A fighter holding an axe cuts through doors and windows faster and does it when checking a noise. The normal courtesy rules still apply.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewIntimidate.en: Walks up on a player, shouts the warning from range, then closes in. The normal warn-before-strike rules still decide when the first blow may land.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewCaution_to.en: Breaks contact early when a few zombies close in, using the existing withdraw behaviour with a lower crowd threshold.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.MeleeCrewCautionCro.en: [Expert] Melee crew: zombies that trigger a retreat
How many zombies near a crew member make it retreat. Normal fighters need five.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieReactSpeed_to.en: How quickly zombies notice and engage NPCs compared with the old pace. 500 is five times faster, 100 is the old pace. Higher values cost a little more processing near NPCs.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieAttackAnims_t.en:
Zombies use the game's bite and scratch attack animations when attacking NPCs.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieScratch_toolt.en: How many of the attacks on a standing NPC are scratches instead of bites.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieDragDown_tool.en:
Enough zombies grabbing one NPC at once drag it down and kill it, with the game's being-eaten voice.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieDragCount_too.en:
Sets how many zombies must grab an NPC at the same time to drag it down. For example, 4 requires four simultaneous attackers.
Default 4.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieDragTime_tool.en: How long the NPC is held down before it dies. 30 is 3 seconds.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcArmorVsZombies.en: [Expert] NPC armour and clothing protection (all hits)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcArmorVsZombies_t.en: The base armour system for NPCs, with the same rules a player gets. It is not a Creator module. Every hit on an NPC (zombie bites and scratches, melee, bullets; from NPCs and from players) rolls against the matching protection of what is worn on the struck body part: bite, scratch or bullet defense. 100 always blocks, 0 never does, layers add up to 100. A blocked hit does no damage and cannot wound or infect, and the clothing tears. Body parts with no protection take the normal damage. Off ignores worn clothing. Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryEnabled_toolt.en:
NPCs that would bleed out can lie injured, be rescued, bandaged or questioned. Off keeps ordinary injury behavior; in multiplayer, only the client controlling the NPC runs its movement.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRescue_toolti.en:
A teammate or friendly ally from the same bloc who can see a downed NPC walks over and bandages it. The rescued NPC stands up limping.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRescueDrag_to.en:
Rescuers drag downed NPCs away before bandaging when zombies or hostiles are within 12 tiles. Off: rescue cannot start with danger that close.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRescueInView_.en:
Allows rescues while players are near or watching. Off: rescuers wait until all players are beyond the nearby-player distance set under expert combat.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRescueRange_t.en: Teammates and friendly members of the same faction this close to the injured NPC may come to help. Helpers outside his squad also need a clear line of sight. Hostile NPCs never rescue him.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryCrawl_tooltip.en:
Downed NPCs crawl away from zombies and hostiles toward their group, and occasionally shuffle instead of lying still.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryAuto_tooltip.en: When an NPC would start bleeding out, this is the chance it goes injured instead. 0 means only the debug menu makes injured NPCs.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryDownHp_toolti.en: Health an NPC has when it goes down injured.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryDeath_tooltip.en: Each question put to an injured NPC can kill it. The player sees that it bled out.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRepPenalty.en: [Expert] Reputation lost for interrogating a non-hostile NPC

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRepPenalty_to.en: Taken once per injured NPC when you question a friendly, neutral or careful one. Hostile NPCs cost nothing.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRepGain.en: [Expert] Reputation gained for bandaging an injured NPC

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRepGain_toolt.en: Small reward for giving a bandage or medical item.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRecover_toolt.en:
Sets the time from getting up with low health to full health and a normal walk. For example, 12 means half a game day of recovery.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryDownHours.en: Unattended time before getting up (game hours)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryDownHours_too.en:
Sets how long a downed NPC waits without help before getting up on its own, still limping. For example, 6 means a quarter of a game day.
Default 4.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRange.en: [Expert] Rescue is blocked within this many tiles of a player

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryRange_tooltip.en: Only used when Rescues happen in front of players is off: then a teammate rescues an injured NPC only when no player is within this range or in sight.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryMultiplayer.en: [Expert] Downed NPC survival on multiplayer servers

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryMultiplayer_t.en:
Lets downed NPCs run on a server with connected players. The client that controls the NPC keeps its own bleed-out timers and wound list; the server only hands it a downed state. Off keeps the ordinary bleed-out in multiplayer. Single player is not affected.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryLeave.en: [Expert] Distance a bandaged NPC walks away (tiles)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.InjuryLeave_tooltip.en: After you bandage an injured NPC it turns neutral and walks this far from you.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BiteLoudness_toolti.en:
Sets the volume of zombie bites, being-eaten voices and NPC pain cries. Sounds fade with distance and are heard only within 25 tiles. At 0, they are muted.
Default 40.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DiscretionEnabled_t.en:
Crews weigh guns, ammo, distance and nearby zombies before attacking a player, and avoid poor odds. Crews sent to attack and NPCs you have hurt still fight.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DiscretionFightPerc.en: A crew fights when its score reaches this value. Lower means bolder crews, higher means more cautious ones. Default 50.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DiscretionLowAmmoRo.en: [Expert] Discretion: rounds counted as low ammunition
A gun with fewer rounds than this (loaded plus reserve) counts as a melee weapon when a crew weighs a fight. Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.DiscretionPatienceS.en: [Expert] Discretion: seconds before a held-back crew commits

A crew that keeps holding back because of the odds alone commits to the fight after this many seconds if you stay near. Crews short on ammunition or surrounded by zombies never commit this way. Default 45.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CalmDownEnabled_too.en:
Careful factions can calm down after provocation once their waiting time passes. Naturally hostile factions and grudges from real attacks do not fade this way.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CalmDownHours_toolt.en: Game hours until a provoked careful faction forgives. Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BlameFair_tooltip.en:
With multiple players, outpost theft blames those inside the outpost rather than everyone. A manhunt keeps its named target instead of switching to the nearest player.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BreachPolicy_toolti.en: NPCs break into a building only when raiding or looting, use an unlocked door first, try a window before smashing a door, and tell before entering a player's base. On by default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieFocusEnabled.en: NPC focus on nearby zombie threats

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieFocusEnabled_.en:
NPCs leave distant zombies alone unless they approach, threaten a friend or are near the NPC's post, helping the group stay on task.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ZombieFocusRadius_t.en: Zombies inside this distance are always fought. Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CautionEnabled_tool.en:
Travelling NPCs avoid zombie groups by skipping buildings, detouring, waiting or backing off. They still fight zombies that are close or coming at them.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CautionAvoidTiles_t.en: How far ahead on their route NPCs watch for zombies. Default 12.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupLifeEnabled.en: [Expert] Group life: spread out, shelter and idle roles

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupLifeEnabled_to.en: Groups walk in a loose formation instead of one clump, never share a square when calm, and when they stop for a rest they move into a nearby house or shelter and idle there with different jobs: one sits in a corner, one keeps watch, two talk face to face, one comments, one stays quiet, others eat or smoke. Danger breaks it up at once. Off restores the old behaviour. On by default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupLifeSpread_too.en: How wide a travelling group spreads out. 100 is the normal formation, 50 keeps them closer, 150 spreads them wider, 0 turns the formation off. Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupLifeShelterIdl.en: Typical length of a group rest, in game minutes. Each rest lasts between half and double of this value. Default 20, so 10 to 40.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupLifeRoles_tool.en: While a group rests, every member gets a role (lookout, sitter, talker, commenter, quiet, eater, smoker) with its own spot and pose. Off: they only spread out and stand. On by default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.StealthEnabled_tool.en: NPCs sometimes sneak (slow, crouched) while moving around town or scavenging. They stop sneaking when they see a player or a hostile NPC. Sneaking NPCs are harder for zombies to notice; the effect follows the zombie sight and hearing settings of the world. On by default.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.StealthFrequency_to.en: Share of the time a calm NPC or group moves sneaking. Higher near zombies. 0 never, 100 always. Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.StealthNotice_toolt.en: How far zombies notice a sneaking NPC, as a share of the normal distance. Poor zombie sight or hearing makes sneaking stronger, eagle sight and pinpoint hearing weaker. Default 50.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineLootPercent_.en:
Groups scavenging away from players keep this share of each house's loot value. They stash it at a base or carry it if homeless. 0 disables this loot gain.
Default 25.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_Events_to.en:
Controls notes, gifts, visitors and attacks at claimed safehouses or buildings you live in. Off disables these base events.
Default Normal (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_Betrayal_.en:
Some visitors may lie about why they came. They give a warning sign before you open the door.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_Attacks_t.en:
Allows groups who hate you to attack your base after warnings. Off prevents these base-event attacks.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_Entry_too.en:
Only when invited: visitors enter after you let them in at the door. Never: all visitors remain outside.
Default Only when invited (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_QuietDays.en: Peace after establishing a base (game days)

Time after a place becomes your base before its first base event can happen.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_Dedicated.en:
Allows base events on dedicated servers while at least one resident is online. Off disables them there. Single player and co-op do not need this switch.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Events_ScriptedEffe.en:
Radio messages, door marks, knocks, distant gunfire and dog barks can happen in the world. Off leaves text notices only.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_NpcQuestions_t.en:
Survivors may ask about your travels or how you cope: up to two questions per talk, then a ten-real-minute cooldown. Not during combat, injury or surrender.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_FollowOptions_.en:
Shows requests for an NPC to follow you or walk alongside you. These conversation choices are still being reworked.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Text_VisitorRangeTi.en:
Visitor and ambient NPC lines show over their heads only within this many tiles, and only if you can see them or stand by the door. 0 shows them at any distance.
Default 14.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Text_Bubbles_toolti.en:
NPC speech appears as a bubble with the speaker's name and a pointer. A speaker off screen gets an edge arrow and the distance. Off: the game's plain floating text.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_StartButton.en: Talk button for waiting visitors and questions

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_StartButton_to.en:
Shows a clickable Talk or Answer button while a visitor waits at your door or someone has just asked you something. Right-click still works.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_UIOpacity.en: Talk window and speech bubble opacity (percent)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_UIOpacity_tool.en:
How solid the talk window and the speech bubble boxes are. Text stays fully opaque. Lower is more see-through, 100 is the classic look.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Text_NpcChatLog.en: NPC lines in the chat box

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Text_NpcChatLog_too.en:
Copies NPC speech into the chat box in multiplayer, or a small log panel in single player. Only on your own screen, rate limited, names follow the stranger rule.
Default Off (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_TraderVis.en:
Travellers may visit your door with goods to trade. Their trading conversation is still being reworked.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Events_RadioActivat.en:
Tunes and switches on a nearby radio for base-event messages, then turns it off. No radio: text only. Requires physical and audible base-event effects.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Events_WallMarks.en: Visible marks beside the front door

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Events_WallMarks_to.en:
Places washable wall marks by the door: up to four, fading after ten game days. Off gives text only. Requires physical and audible base-event effects.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Reputation_Professi.en:
Uses each faction's view of your profession when choosing nearby encounters. Off: every profession uses that faction's general attitude.
Default on.

During the first week, NPCs from a similar background may recognise your former profession, such as police recognising police. Requires personal reputation.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_InviteMin.en:
Time an invited visitor waits for the door to open before giving up.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_VisitorHo.en: Visitor's initial wait at the door (real seconds)

Visitors face the door and wait for roughly two thirds to four thirds of this duration. Opening the door, talking or attacking ends it immediately. At 0, no initial wait.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_KnockSoun.en: Knocks for visitors, door sound for break-ins

Visitors knock at your door or window and you hear it from up to about 50 tiles, instead of a text notice. A door sound plays only when someone breaks into your house and opens the first door inside. Off: text notice only.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_SquatPerc.en:
Chance that an overnight guest refuses to leave in the morning until you talk them out.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_BittenPer.en:
Chance that a wounded visitor is secretly bitten. Bitten visitors refuse to be searched.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_LadderGap.en: Time between hostile warning stages (game hours)

Minimum time between a hostile group's threat letter, door mark, sabotage and eventual attack.
Default 48.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_BaseFlag_.en:
In SP/co-op, recognised bases block NPC spawning, shelter, loot and uninvited non-hostiles. Off: any slept-in or built-at place blocks spawns, as on dedicated servers.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_BaseScore.en:
Points needed to recognise a base, with at least two kinds of evidence. A night adds 20, a day there 10, a running generator 20 and a claim 30.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_ChancePer.en:
Chance of an event at an eligible house. Rare halves this chance; Often increases it by half.
Default 12.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_CheckHour.en:
Time between event checks at the same house.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_GapDays.en: Minimum time between base events (game days)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_GapDays_t.en:
Minimum gap between events at one house. Rare doubles the gap; Often halves it, but never below one game day.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_VisitGapD.en:
Minimum gap between two visits to the same house.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_AttackGap.en: Minimum time between base attacks (game days)

Minimum gap between attacks on the same house.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_AttackMin.en:
World age before the first attack on a house is allowed.
Default 14.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_DensityMi.en: Zombie count for armed visitors only (zombies)

Above this many zombies within 40 tiles of the front door, only armed groups visit.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_DensityHi.en:
Above this many zombies within 40 tiles of the front door, nobody visits and notes arrive half as often.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_DensityEx.en:
Above this many zombies within 40 tiles of the front door, nothing is left at the house.
Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_AwayTiles.en:
Notes and gifts can be left when every resident is at least this far from the delivery point and is not looking toward it.
Default 40.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_HiddenTil.en:
Notes and gifts can also be left when every resident is at least this far away, is not looking toward the delivery point and cannot see it.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_DropDeadl.en:
How long a note waits for a safe delivery opportunity before it expires without being delivered.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Safehouse_MailboxTi.en:
Notes go into a mailbox within this distance of the front door. Without one, they are left on the porch.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesEnabled_t.en:
Crews can move on after an encounter, such as fixing a car then scavenging from it. Distant groups plan around supplies. Off: crews keep their earlier behavior.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesSwitchCha.en:
Sets the share of finished encounters whose crews take up another activity. The rest keep their post and later leave as before; higher values put more crews on roads.
Default 70.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesNeedsDrai.en:
Scales how quickly groups become hungry and thirsty. Higher values cause more supply runs and more chances to encounter you.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesAdoptCap_.en:
Caps encounter crews kept travelling while you are away; they share the distant-group limit. Extra crews may continue while you are near, then leave the world as before.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesFixedCarD.en:
On: repaired cars have working engines, batteries, bonnets and some fuel, and remain with their trunk loot. Off: the car stays a wreck but remains the crew's stash.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesFixedCarF.en: Repaired encounter car fuel (percent of tank)

Sets how full a repaired car's fuel tank is. For example, 25 gives it a quarter tank.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesHunting_t.en:
Allows armed NPC crews to hunt. Offline only allows hunting away from players and leaves nearby wildlife to you.
Default Offline and nearby wildlife (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesSwitchHou.en: Wait before abandoning a car (game hours)

A crew stuck at a broken or crashed car this long may leave it and go scavenging, but only when no player is nearby.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesSwitchCle.en:
A crew cannot abandon its car while any player is closer than this distance. For example, 80 keeps it at the car while you are within 80 tiles.
Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesBases_too.en:
Crews of two or more may settle in an empty building away from players, store their loot and return after trips.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesMaxBases_.en:
Caps settled NPC bases across the world. If the limit is exceeded, the oldest base is abandoned. At 0, crews cannot found new bases.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesPartyWeig.en:
Scales encounters with fishers, hunters, foragers, woodcutters, camp builders, scavengers and water carriers. 100 keeps the usual rate; 0 disables these encounters.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesBaseChanc.en:
Chance that each eligible crew founds a base, checked once per game day.
Default 25.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesBaseRetur.en: NPC trip length before returning home (game hours)

Time a crew with a base spends away before planning a return home.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesBaseClear.en: New NPC base distance from players (tiles)

Minimum distance from any player when an NPC crew founds a base.
Default 45.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesHuntYield.en: NPC hunting food yield (percent of normal)

Scales food gained from NPC hunts. 100 keeps the usual amount; 0 gives no food and 200 gives twice the usual amount.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesFishing_t.en:
Allows NPC crews to fish near water without reducing the fish available to players.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesFishingMi.en:
Sessions last 60-140 percent of this time. Fishers stop if noticed by a player, hostile or zombie, or after gunfire or a hit.
Default 65.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesFishYield.en:
Scales fish caught by NPC crews. 100 keeps the usual catch; 0 gives no fish and 200 gives twice the usual catch.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesForaging_.en:
Foraging crews bring seasonal berries, herbs, nuts and mushrooms to their camp stash. This does not reduce what players can forage.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ActivitiesForageYie.en:
Scales food foraged per crew per game day. 100 gives six items, 200 gives twelve and 0 gives none.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PartyEnabled_toolti.en:
Lets you ask a friendly NPC group to take you in. The group keeps its own plans, offers jobs and warnings, and can leave you behind if you stay away.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PartyMaxSize_toolti.en:
A group at this size refuses new members. NPCs and players both count toward the limit.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PartyMinOpinion_too.en:
Sets the leader's minimum opinion of you before you can join. Soldiers and raiders require more; gentler groups, such as families, require less.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PartyTaskFrequency_.en:
Sets the minimum time between jobs offered by your group leader at calm stops. At 0, automatic offers stop; you can still ask for a job.
Default 45.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PartyAwayMinutes_to.en:
Sets how long you can stay far from your NPC group before it leaves you behind and your membership ends.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PartyStories_toolti.en:
Allows settled groups near you to tell stories about their old lives. You can also ask for a story.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PlansEnabled_toolti.en:
Free groups choose goals such as supplies or shelter, discuss them and follow through until done, blocked, hurt or threatened. Off: groups return to roaming and idling.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PlansRadius_tooltip.en:
Sets how far a group looks for a building to visit for its plan. Nearby buildings are preferred; 80 limits the search to 80 tiles.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PlansLifespanHours_.en:
Sets how long a group keeps a plan before giving up and choosing again. Shelter plans last until morning.
Default 6.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PlansTalk_tooltip.en:
Groups discuss plans before leaving and speak when they arrive or give up. Off: they still follow plans, but silently.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunsVsZombiesPercen.en: How often an NPC that could shoot a zombie does so. Gunfire draws more zombies, so by default NPCs walk around zombies, use melee on a lone one, and keep their guns for NPCs and players. They still shoot when cornered, hurt, defending a hurt player, on a horde that blocks the way, or on duty as military or police. 0 means never unless cornered. 100 is the old behaviour. Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunNoiseZombies.en: [Expert] No gunfire with this many zombies near

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunNoiseZombies_too.en: An NPC holds fire when more than this many zombies are within 25 tiles, unless it is cornered, hurt or defending a hurt player. 0 turns the check off. Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunHordeSize.en: [Expert] Horde size that may be shot

Sandbox_ProjectALife.GunHordeSize_toolti.en: A group of at least this many zombies within 12 tiles that blocks an NPC's route may be shot at, if it is not too loud (see the noise limit). Default 5.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SeedPerTown_tooltip.en:
Sets how many roaming groups each town receives when the world starts. The distant roaming group limit may allow extra groups in larger worlds.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SeedClearTiles_tool.en:
Prevents starting roaming groups from being placed this close to a player. Groups may still arrive later. At 0, this starting clearance is disabled.
Default 150.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.NeighbourGroups_too.en:
Blocks new roaming groups when this many already live within 240 tiles. From day 4, the limit drops by one but never below one.
Default 4.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HibernateTiles_tool.en:
Beyond this distance (60-400 tiles), groups stop travelling, planning and using supplies. Members and loot stay; groups wake on approach without catching up missed time.
Default 150.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RespawnCooldownDays.en: Local replacement delay after deaths (game days)

Blocks new roaming groups in an area of about 120 tiles after NPC deaths. Heavy losses extend the delay. At 0, this delay is disabled.
Default 3.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RegrowthDays.en: Local recovery interval (game days per group)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RegrowthDays_toolti.en:
After the death cooldown, limits a recovering area to one new group per interval. At 0, this additional recovery limit is disabled.
Default 2.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnFairnessEnable.en:
Keeps spawning, waking and removal away from nearby or watching players. Also reduces rural encounters and prevents checkpoints near players or on dead-end roads.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnKeepOutTiles_t.en:
Keeps random groups from appearing this close or in view. Countryside adds 20 tiles; loaded-map limits still apply. Groups appear outside the clearance and walk in.
Default 70.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnStartGraceMinu.en:
Lets welcome and starting-town groups appear nearby during a new character's first minutes. Other groups still obey the normal player clearance.
Default 10.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LifecycleReloadGuar.en:
Restores NPCs after map reloads, removes leftover zombie copies out of sight and clears zombies around returning groups. Blocked groups return farther away. Off removes this protection.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnDespawnMinTile.en:
NPCs can become inactive or be removed only when they are at least this far from every player and out of sight.
Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnRuralDensity.en: Countryside encounter rate (percent of town rate)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnRuralDensity_t.en:
Sets open-countryside encounters relative to towns. At 50, the rate is half the town rate. Only suitable visitors, such as travellers and hunters, appear.
Default 50.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnWildernessDens.en: Wilderness encounter rate (percent of town rate)

Sets forest and wilderness encounters relative to towns. At 30, the rate is 30 percent of the town rate.
Default 30.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnFarmDensity.en: Farmland encounter rate (percent of town rate)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnFarmDensity_to.en:
Sets farm and ranch encounters relative to towns. At 60, the rate is 60 percent of the town rate.
Default 60.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.SpawnCheckpointMinT.en: Blockades and checkpoints are never built within this distance of a player, a player base or a place a player drove through in the last five minutes, and never on dead-end roads. Default 150.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BloodEnabled_toolti.en:
Adds floor splatter, bleeding drips and death pools, respecting the game's blood settings. Off: only the game's ordinary splatter and body stains remain.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BloodPercent_toolti.en:
Scales floor splatter, body stains, drips and pools from non-melee deaths. At 100, only the earlier body-stain behavior remains.
Default 200.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.BloodMeleeKillPerce.en: [Expert] NPC blood when killed in melee (%%)
Size of the blood pool when an NPC is killed with a blade, bat or other melee weapon, and the blood on the attacker. Only used while the NPC blood amount is above 100%%. Default 300%%.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingEnabled_tool.en:
Allows NPCs to react to world sounds and notice nearby players who run or shoot.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingRadiusPercen.en:
Scales how far NPCs hear sounds. At 50, hearing distance is halved. Indoor player sounds and NPC gunshots use half the resulting range.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingWallPercent_.en:
Sets how much hearing distance remains when a wall blocks the sound's path. At 50, a blocked sound can be heard from half as far away.
Default 50.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingFloorPercent.en:
Reduces hearing distance for each floor between the NPC and sound. At 50, one floor leaves half the range; two floors leave one quarter.
Default 50.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingPeripheralTi.en:
Lets NPCs notice a running or recently shooting player behind them on the same floor. At 0, this rear detection is disabled.
Default 8.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingAlertSeconds.en:
Sets how long extra awareness from sounds and warnings lasts before the NPC returns to its normal awareness.
Default 20.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.HearingAlertPercent.en:
Sets the minimum awareness after an NPC hears a sound. Confirmed contacts and final warnings still give full awareness.
Default 70.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CautionDangerRoutin.en: Walking NPCs take short detours around nearby zombie crowds and fresh combat or loud noises. They wait or abandon an unsafe destination when no safe detour is found. Running and combat movement keep their existing rules.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CautionHazardCheck_.en: Checks proposed movement legs for burning tiles, lit campfires and water. NPCs reject legs with known hazards. Applies to all movement paces.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CautionDangerRays.en: Danger avoidance sight checks (per real second)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CautionDangerRays_t.en:
Limits extra sight checks for danger detours across all NPCs. Groups wait when the limit is reached. At 0, these extra checks stop; normal perception is unaffected.
Default 32.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.FireManeuver_toolti.en: Shooters can advance to nearby cover and briefly step out to fire. Eligible squad gunners provide bounded covering fire. Turning this off cancels active maneuvers.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.ForwardCoverTiles_t.en: Maximum length of a forward cover leg. Default 4; range 2-6. Weapon distance and movement safety still apply.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PeekWindow_tooltip.en: Time at the firing point before returning to cover. Default 1200; range 600-2000. At most two shots; weapon cycles finish normally.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.PinWindow_tooltip.en: Maximum covering fire time for one squad maneuver. Default 4000; range 2000-6000. Requires an eligible gunner and a clear friendly-safe line.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.RetreatLOS_tooltip.en: Prefer nearby retreat destinations that hide the NPC from the threat. Existing retreat triggers, stamina and fallback destinations remain in use.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatJeemResidents.en: Expose living Jeem residents as residents through the A-Life compatibility API when the Jeem extension is active. Needs an available actor registry. Does not replace the Companion Dogs patch. Applied at world startup; restart after changing this.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatPointBlank_to.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when Point Blank is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatWanderingZomb.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when Wandering Zombies is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatCyesPushDoors.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when Cye's Push Doors is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatMoreTraits_to.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when More Traits Definitive is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatProjectExile_.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when Project Exile is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatPixelStrike_t.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when Pixel Strike Indicator is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatGaelGunStore_.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when GaelGunStore-Firearms is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatAutoAll_toolt.en: Enable the A-Life compatibility adapter when Auto All is active. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Turning it off disables only this adapter, not the other mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatCryOfFear_too.en: Let Cry of Fear monsters bite A-Life people when their own attack animation never starts, at the same pace as ordinary zombies. Applied once at world startup; restart after changing this. Does nothing without the monsters mod.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatNoPocketLoot.en: [Expert] No pocket loot on A-Life people

Sandbox_ProjectALife.CompatNoPocketLoot_.en:
Mark A-Life people as already searched when they appear, so the vanilla zombie pocket loot is not rolled on their bodies. Off keeps the vanilla loot. Use it with mods that add loot to zombies.
Default off.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsBuildBudget.en:
Maximum work units per round. Higher values finish sooner but may increase server stalls. Multiplayer streaming pauses still apply.
Default 250.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsMaxCompound.en:
Limits new walled compounds. At 0, none are proposed. Existing sites, small camps, checkpoints and admin-built sites stay.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsCompoundSpa.en:
Minimum distance between new walled compounds. Recently expired sites count until cleared. Small camps and fixed checkpoints are unchanged.
Default 500.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsLightsOn_to.en:
Keeps campfires, lamps and generators in outposts, compounds, checkpoints and camps burning and switched on, refuelled while a player is near. Off leaves them as built.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcDropPercent.en: NPC loot: how much of their gear stays on bodies (percent)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcDropPercent_.en:
Chance that each item an NPC carried stays on its body. 100 means everything they carried drops (the default); lower values leave emptier bodies. Use the wear setting below to make drops poorer instead. A fixed NPC weapon drop chance overrides this for weapons.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcWearPercent.en: NPC loot: how worn out dropped gear is (percent)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcWearPercent_.en:
Gear on NPC bodies comes out used up: many guns are broken or nearly so, magazines are almost empty, clothes and vests are tattered, loose ammo is scarce. NPCs still fight with working weapons while alive; the wear is applied when they die. 0 leaves everything pristine, 100 is full wear.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcWeaponPercen.en: [Expert] NPC loot: weapons (percent of the loot setting)

Multiplies the NPC loot percent for guns and melee weapons. Ignored while NPC weapon drop chance is a fixed choice. For example, 50 halves weapon drops.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcArmorPercent.en: [Expert] NPC loot: armor and clothing (percent of the loot setting)

Multiplies the NPC loot percent for worn armor and clothing, including rare armor. For example, 50 halves armor drops.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcAmmoPercent.en: [Expert] NPC loot: magazines and ammo (percent of the loot setting)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcAmmoPercent_.en:
Multiplies the NPC loot percent for dropped magazines and loose ammo. For example, 50 halves ammo drops.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.LootNpcSuppliesPerc.en: [Expert] NPC loot: supplies and other items (percent of the loot setting)

Multiplies the NPC loot percent for food, medicine, tools and pocket items; identity cards always stay. For example, 50 halves supply drops.
Default 100.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Persons_to.en:
Door visits bring named individuals and small groups with their own history, needs and conversation. Off: visits work exactly as before.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_ProactiveE.en: Guests speak up on their own

How often a guest inside your home starts talking by themselves, for example asking about the TV. Rare waits longer, Often waits less. Off: guests only answer when you talk.
Default Normal (3).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_EventMinGa.en: Shortest pause between a guest's own questions (real seconds)

Real seconds that must pass after a guest speaks up before the same player is prompted again. Higher is calmer.
Default 240.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_StayHours.en: Longest stay of a guest (game hours)

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_StayHours_.en:
A guest never stays inside longer than this. Most guests leave sooner. Raise it to let people ask to stay for a few nights; more time inside means more risk and more help.
Default 1.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Parties.en: Couples, families and small groups arrive together

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Parties_to.en:
Pairs and trios of related people can knock together instead of one stranger at a time. Off: one visitor per visit.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_ReturningC.en: Chance that a visitor you befriended comes back (percent)

Once you have really helped someone, this chance decides whether a later visit is that person coming back. 0 means never.
Default 15.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Life.en: Guests move about, sit, read and look out of windows

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Life_toolt.en:
Guests inside your home walk around, sit on furniture, read and look out of windows instead of standing where they were let in. Off: they stand still.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_ChangeClot.en:
Adult guests can ask for clean clothes and change in a closed room, down to the default body and never beyond. Off: no clothes changes.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Privacy.en: Privacy when a guest changes clothes

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Privacy_to.en:
Strict: a guest only changes in a room with the door shut, and not while you stand near the door. Normal: the door may be open.
Default Strict (1).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Flirt_tool.en:
Adult guests can show gentle, optional, non-explicit warmth after real trust and always accept a no. Off: no flirting at all.
Default On (2).

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Books.en: Guests read books and talk about them

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Books_tool.en:
Guests can carry and read books and newspapers and discuss them with you. Off: no book conversations.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_ChatMirror.en: Show guest speech in the chat box

Words spoken by guests also appear in the chat window, not only as speech bubbles. Needs the chat mirror of the talk interface.
Default on.

Sandbox_ProjectALife.Visitors_Debug_tool.en:
Adds extra visitor lines to the QA dump and the flight recorder to help find problems. Leave off for normal play.
Default off.
